items.body: ### Issue Title **`hermes gateway start` pops up cmd.exe console window on Windows (uv venv + pythonw shim issue)** --- ### Description When running `hermes gateway start` on Windows with Hermes installed via `pip` in a **uv-created virtual environment**, the gateway pops up a visible `cmd.exe` console window instead of running silently in the background. ### Root Cause The problem is in the generated `Hermes_Gateway.cmd` script located at `%HERMES_HOME%/gateway-service/Hermes_Gateway.cmd`. The script references `venv/Scripts/pythonw.exe` as the interpreter: ```cmd C:\Users\...\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run ``` However, when the venv is created by `uv`, the `venv/Scripts/pythonw.exe` is a **uv-generated shim launcher** (~44KB), not a real `pythonw.exe`. This shim internally spawns the **base `python.exe`** (not `pythonw.exe`), which has a console subsystem and creates a visible terminal window. **Evidence:** - uv shim size: ~44KB (confirmed via `pyvenv.cfg` containing `uv = 0.11.15`) - Real pythonw.exe size: ~90KB (located at `uv/python/cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none/pythonw.exe`) ### Existing Code That Handles This (but not used by .cmd generation) The module `hermes_cli/gateway_windows.py` already contains `_resolve_detached_python()` (line ~474) that detects uv-managed venvs and resolves to the **base** `pythonw.exe`: ```python def _resolve_detached_python(python_exe: str) -> tuple[str, Path, list[str]]: # ... reads pyvenv.cfg cfg = _read_pyvenv_cfg(venv_dir) home = cfg.get("home", "") if "uv" in cfg and home: base_pythonw = Path(home) / "pythonw.exe" site_packages = venv_dir / "Lib" / "site-packages" if base_pythonw.exists() and site_packages.exists(): return (str(base_pythonw), venv_dir, [str(site_packages)]) return (windowed, venv_dir, []) ``` This is correctly used in `_spawn_detached()` and `_build_gateway_argv()` (for direct subprocess.Popen spawns), but **NOT** in `_build_gateway_cmd_script()` (line ~294), which generates the `.cmd` file for the Scheduled Task. ### Affected Code **File:** `hermes_cli/gateway_windows.py` Function `_build_gateway_cmd_script()` at line ~294: ```python def _build_gateway_cmd_script( python_path: str, # <-- this is venv/Scripts/python.exe working_dir: str, hermes_home: str, profile_arg: str, ) -> str: ... pythonw_path = _derive_venv_pythonw(python_path) # <-- only looks for sibling pythonw.exe in venv/Scripts ... ``` `_derive_venv_pythonw()` only checks for a sibling `pythonw.exe` at the same directory level. It does NOT inspect `pyvenv.cfg` to detect uv-managed venvs. ### Proposed Fix In `_build_gateway_cmd_script()`, use `_resolve_detached_python()` (or equivalent logic) instead of `_derive_venv_pythonw()` to get the correct windowless python interpreter. When uv is detected, also add `PYTHONPATH` to the generated `.cmd` so the base interpreter can find venv site-packages. **Current (broken) generated .cmd:** ```cmd set "VIRTUAL_ENV=C:\...\hermes-agent\venv" C:\...\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run # uv shim → pops up console ``` **Expected (fixed) generated .cmd:** ```cmd set "VIRTUAL_ENV=C:\...\hermes-agent\venv" set "PYTHONPATH=C:\...\hermes-agent;C:\...\venv\Lib\site-packages" C:\Users\...\AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\pythonw.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run # real pythonw → no console ``` ### Environment - **OS:** Windows 10/11 - **Hermes version:** v0.14.0 - **Python:** 3.11.15 (installed via uv) - **Virtual environment:** Created by uv (`pyvenv.cfg` contains `uv = 0.11.15`) - **Install method:** `pip install hermes-agent` into uv venv ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Install Python via uv, create a venv 2. `pip install hermes-agent` 3. `hermes gateway install` (accept all prompts) 4. `hermes gateway start` 5. A `cmd.exe` console window appears and stays visible ### Workaround Manually edit the generated `.cmd` file to use the base `pythonw.exe` and add `PYTHONPATH`: ```cmd set "PYTHONPATH=C:\...\hermes-agent;C:\...\hermes-agent\venv\Lib\site-packages" C:\Users\...\AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\pythonw.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run ``` --- *This issue was drafted by [WorkBuddy](https://www.codebuddy.cn) AI assistant, based on diagnostic analysis performed with the reporter.*

items.title: xAI OAuth/SuperGrok Responses API rejects replayed encrypted reasoning — 400 on every multi-turn tool call (regression from b4afc6546)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

On the xAI OAuth/SuperGrok backend (`provider: xai-oauth`, `grok-4.3`, `codex_responses` transport), **every multi-turn request that replays a prior assistant turn containing encrypted reasoning fails** with HTTP 400:

```
Error code: 400 - {'code': 'Client specified an invalid argument',
'error': 'Invalid request content: Each message must have at least one content element.'}
```

The first turn succeeds; the follow-up turn (which replays the prior turn's reasoning) 400s. This breaks every cron job that uses tools, and any multi-turn chat where the model reasons and then calls a tool.

## Environment

- `provider: xai-oauth` (SuperGrok), `model: grok-4.3`
- transport `codex_responses`, endpoint `https://api.x.ai/v1/responses`
- Observed around HEAD `ba9964ff0`; the relevant files are unchanged on current `main`.

## Root cause

`b4afc6546` ("fix(xai): restore encrypted reasoning replay across turns") removed the `is_xai_responses` gate in `_chat_messages_to_responses_input` (`agent/codex_responses_adapter.py`). The xAI OAuth/SuperGrok `/v1/responses` surface rejects replayed `encrypted_content` reasoning items minted by prior turns — exactly what PR #26644 originally gated against.

Two committed pieces combine to produce the rejected payload:

- `agent/transports/codex.py` — for xAI, `kwargs["include"] = ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` (asks xAI to echo encrypted reasoning back to us).
- `agent/codex_responses_adapter.py` (`_chat_messages_to_responses_input`) — replays those `codex_reasoning_items` on the next turn with **no** `is_xai_responses` gate.

Resulting turn-2 `input` array:

```
[user, reasoning, reasoning, assistant(content=""), function_call, function_call_output]
```

which xAI rejects.

## Reproduction

1. `provider: xai-oauth`, `model: grok-4.3`, any `reasoning_effort` other than `none`.
2. A prompt that makes the model reason and then call a tool (e.g. a cron job that uses `x_search` / `web`).
3. The follow-up request after the tool result returns HTTP 400 "Each message must have at least one content element."

Verified by running the committed `_chat_messages_to_responses_input` at HEAD with `is_xai_responses=True` against such a history — it emits the replayed reasoning items (plus an empty assistant message), reproducing the rejected payload.

## Evidence (regression)

- Runs **before** `b4afc6546` (no replay): success.
- Runs **after** `b4afc6546` (replay on): consistent 400 on multi-turn tool calls.

## Secondary issue (same error, independent)

When an assistant turn has reasoning but no text, the adapter emits `{"role": "assistant", "content": ""}` as the required "following item" after a reasoning item. xAI also rejects empty-content messages with the same error. This empty message should be skipped when `function_call` items already follow (they satisfy the "following item" requirement).

## Suggested fix

Restore the `is_xai_responses` gate on the reasoning-replay loop (and skip the empty assistant message when tool calls follow). If the partner integration genuinely requires replay on the **API-key** xAI surface, distinguish OAuth from API-key rather than enabling replay for all `is_xai_responses`.

## Workaround

Setting `agent.reasoning_effort: none` avoids the bug (no `include` echo is requested, so there is nothing to replay), at the cost of cross-turn reasoning threading. grok-4.3 still reasons natively server-side.

items.title: single-key auth errors should fail fast instead of retrying max_retries times

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

When a user has only **one API key** configured (no credential pool with rotation), an `auth` error (HTTP 401/403) triggers the full retry loop instead of failing fast.

### Current behavior

1. API call fails with 401
2. `error_classifier.py` classifies as `auth` (retryable=True)
3. `_recover_with_credential_pool()` has no backup keys to rotate to → returns False
4. Falls back to generic retry logic: `jittered_backoff(5s → 120s)` × `max_retries`
5. Each retry hits the same single expired/deprecated key → same 401
6. All retries are wasted — API calls + backoff delay, then eventually gives up

### Expected behavior

When there is only **one credential** in the pool (or no credential pool at all), an `auth` error should:
- Try a single **fresh connection** (in case it was a transient auth hiccup)
- If it fails again → immediately classify as `auth_permanent` (retryable=False)
- Surface a clear error message: "Your API key appears to be invalid/expired. Try `hermes config set provider.api_key ...` or add a backup key via `hermes auth add`."

### Why it matters

- Wastes API calls on dead keys (up to `max_retries` invocations × backoff)
- Delays user getting actionable error feedback
- In gateway mode, the 5-120s backoff per retry makes the agent appear hung

### Affected users

Anyone using a **single API key** who runs into an expired/revoked key. This is the most common deployment pattern (single .env key, no credential pool).

## Proposed solution

In `conversation_loop.py`, after calling `_recover_with_credential_pool()` returns `False`:

```python
# If credential pool had nothing to rotate to, treat auth as permanent
if not recovered_with_pool and classified.is_auth:
    if not transient_auth_retry_attempted:
        transient_auth_retry_attempted = True
        continue  # One retry with a fresh connection to rule out transient
    # Second failure → permanent
    classified = ClassifiedError(
        reason=FailoverReason.auth_permanent,
        retryable=False,
        message="API key appears invalid after retry — check your .env or run `hermes auth add`",
    )
    # Fall through to the retryable=False abort path below
```

This adds at most **one extra API call** (fresh connection), then immediately surfaces the error.

## Alternative considered

- **Check pool size upfront**: Also valid, but requires knowing the pool cardinality at the error-site, which is one more coupling point.

---

*Reported by a user who hit this with an expired DeepSeek API key. The system correctly identified the 401 but burned multiple retries before giving up.*

items.title: bug(gateway): /restart fails in container environments — "No such file or directory: bash" during detached restart

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Description

When running Hermes Agent inside a Docker container (no systemd), executing `/restart` causes the gateway to shut down cleanly but **fail to respawn**. The error log shows:

```
ERROR gateway.run: Failed to launch detached gateway restart: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: bash
```

The gateway then stays down until manually restarted or the container is recycled.

## Root Cause

In `gateway/run.py:_launch_detached_restart_command()` (line ~3203–3213), the detached restart subprocess is spawned with a bare `"bash"` command:

```python
subprocess.Popen(
    ["bash", "-lc", shell_cmd],
    stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    start_new_session=True,
)
```

Note that `setsid` (used in the same method) is resolved via `shutil.which("setsid")` and works reliably, but `bash` is hardcoded as a bare name.

During graceful shutdown, `_kill_tool_subprocesses("post-interrupt")` runs just before the restart attempt. In container environments where processes share restricted execution contexts, `subprocess.Popen(["bash", ...])` can fail because the process environment may be altered during shutdown cleanup.

## Impact

- Gateway goes down after `/restart` and does not come back up automatically
- User must manually intervene (restart container, or run `hermes gateway run --replace` from inside the container)
- Affects any non-systemd deployment: Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Termux/Android, etc.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes Agent in a Docker container without systemd
2. Send `/restart` command to the gateway
3. Observe: gateway shuts down cleanly but new instance never starts
4. Check `gateway-restart.log` for the `Failed to launch detached gateway restart` error

## Environment

- Hermes v0.14.0
- Docker container (Linux x64, 2 CPU, 4GB RAM)
- No systemd
- Uptime: 5+ days

## Suggested Fix

Replace the bare `"bash"` with a path resolved by `shutil.which("bash")` (same pattern already used for `setsid_bin` on the line above):

```python
bash_bin = shutil.which("bash")
if bash_bin:
    subprocess.Popen(
        [setsid_bin or bash_bin, bash_bin, "-lc", shell_cmd],
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        start_new_session=True,
    )
```

This is a minimal 2-line change that mirrors the existing `setsid` resolution pattern.

## Related Issues

- #16621, #17576 — propose replacing the bash restart watcher entirely with a Python-based approach
- #29603 — gateway restart kills new instance on non-systemd environments
- #29619 — respawn via Python watcher
- #25263 (closed) — restart via service in containers

## Problem

The `/sessions` slash command is registered in `COMMAND_REGISTRY` (hermes_cli/commands.py) and included in `GATEWAY_KNOWN_COMMANDS`, but the gateway dispatch in `gateway/run.py` has no handler for it.

As a result, when a user sends `/sessions` via gateway (WeChat, Telegram, etc.), the command is recognized as a known command so it doesn't trigger "Unknown command", but there's no dispatch branch to handle it — the message falls through and gets sent to the AI as regular chat.

## Root Cause

Commit `09a491464` (2026-05-06) added `/sessions` to `COMMAND_REGISTRY` and implemented the TUI frontend (`ui-tui/src/app/slash/commands/session.ts`), but never added the corresponding handler in `gateway/run.py`.

CLI has `_handle_sessions_command` (cli.py:6380) with a dispatch branch at line 8001-8002, but gateway is missing both.

## Reproduction

1. Send `/sessions` via any gateway platform (WeChat, Telegram, etc.)
2. Expected: list recent sessions or allow resuming
3. Actual: message is treated as regular chat and forwarded to the LLM

## Fix

Two changes needed in `gateway/run.py`:

1. Add dispatch branch (after `resume`, around line 7280):
```python
if canonical == "sessions":
    return await self._handle_sessions_command(event)
```

2. Implement `_handle_sessions_command` method (mirrors CLI behavior):
- Bare `/sessions` or `/sessions list` → list recent sessions
- `/sessions <id_or_title>` → delegate to `/resume`

## Verification

Tested on gateway (WeChat): `/sessions` now correctly lists recent sessions and `/sessions <id>` resumes the target session.

items.body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes saves the OAuth token to `~/.hermes/.env`, it does not wrap the value in quotes. If the token contains a `#` character, everything after it is treated as a comment by the `.env` parser, resulting in a truncated and invalid token.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes model` and choose Claude Pro/Max (OAuth)
2. Paste a token that contains a `#` character
3. Hermes saves the token unquoted to `~/.hermes/.env`
4. The token gets truncated at `#`, causing a 401 authentication error

## Expected Behavior

Token values should be quoted when written to `.env`:
```
ANTHROPIC_TOKEN="sk-ant-oat01-..."
```
so that special characters like `#` are preserved.

## Actual Behavior

```
ANTHROPIC_TOKEN=abc123#xyz456
```
Only `abc123` is read — everything after `#` is treated as a comment — causing HTTP 401 authentication errors.

## Workaround

Manually set the token with quotes:
```bash
hermes config set ANTHROPIC_TOKEN "sk-ant-oat01-..."
```

## Platform

Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu)

items.title: PRD: Deepen gateway media delivery into one routing module
items.body:
## PRD: Deepen gateway media delivery into one routing module

### Source
Daily architecture-review automation (`source:architecture-review`).

### Prior proposal check
No prior GitHub issues labelled `source:architecture-review` were found in this repository. I also checked for nearby existing issues and found individual symptoms such as background task media delivery and platform voice/media bugs, but not a proposal for the underlying Module seam.

### Context and ADR check
- `CONTEXT.md`: not present in this checkout.
- `docs/adr/`: not present in this checkout.
- Relevant project vocabulary from `AGENTS.md`: gateway runner, platform adapters, cron scheduler, delivery, messaging platform integrations.

### Problem
Gateway media delivery is currently a shallow collection of repeated routing decisions spread across multiple Modules:

- `gateway/platforms/base.py` owns `BasePlatformAdapter.extract_media()`, `extract_local_files()`, `should_send_media_as_audio()`, and the normal adapter delivery path.
- `cron/scheduler.py` mirrors adapter routing with local `_VIDEO_EXTS` / `_IMAGE_EXTS`, imports `should_send_media_as_audio()`, and explicitly chooses `send_voice`, `send_video`, `send_image_file`, or `send_document`.
- `gateway/run.py` has another attachment path for kanban/background task artifacts with its own `_IMAGE_EXTS` / `_VIDEO_EXTS` and a different batching rule.
- Platform-specific delivery facts leak into shared code: Telegram audio/voice constraints live in `BasePlatformAdapter`; Matrix/Slack/QQBot symptoms have their own issue-level fixes.

The current Interface is nearly as complex as the Implementation: each caller must know extension sets, voice-vs-audio distinctions, batching behavior, metadata/threading, fallback-to-document behavior, and platform quirks. Applying the deletion test, deleting any one helper would not concentrate complexity; it would reappear in the callers that already partially duplicate it.

### Goal
Create a deeper gateway media delivery Module so callers ask for “deliver these media artifacts for this platform/session” instead of recreating routing policy at each call site.

### Non-goals
- Do not change platform adapter behavior in the first pass except where tests prove parity.
- Do not redesign the whole gateway command or session architecture.
- Do not replace existing adapter send methods (`send_voice`, `send_video`, etc.); the new Module should orchestrate them.

### Proposed solution
Introduce a gateway media delivery Module behind a single seam used by:

1. Normal gateway responses in `BasePlatformAdapter`.
2. Cron delivery in `cron/scheduler.py`.
3. Background/kanban artifact delivery in `gateway/run.py`.

The Module should own:

- Media classification from local paths and `MEDIA:` tags.
- Platform-specific routing policy such as Telegram voice/audio constraints.
- Image batching vs single-file sends.
- Fallback rules when a platform-specific sender is unsupported or fails.
- Metadata/thread propagation so all delivery paths preserve the same reply/thread semantics.
- A small test surface around routing decisions and adapter calls.

Platform adapters remain concrete Adapters at the seam: the media delivery Module decides *what* to call; each platform adapter decides *how* to perform that send.

### Benefits
- **Locality:** media routing bugs move to one Module instead of being fixed separately in gateway runner, platform base, cron delivery, and individual platform paths.
- **Leverage:** callers get platform-correct attachment delivery through a smaller Interface; they no longer need to know extension sets, batching rules, or Telegram/Matrix/Slack quirks.
- **Testability:** routing can be tested with fake adapters and table-driven cases: image batch, video, voice audio, non-voice audio, unknown extension fallback, thread metadata preservation, and failure fallback.
- **AI-navigability:** future agents can find the delivery policy in one obvious place instead of bouncing between `gateway/run.py`, `gateway/platforms/base.py`, and `cron/scheduler.py`.

### Acceptance criteria
- One shared media delivery Module is used by cron delivery, background/kanban artifact delivery, and the normal gateway response path.
- Duplicate `_IMAGE_EXTS` / `_VIDEO_EXTS` definitions are removed from gateway runner and cron call sites, or replaced with imports from the media delivery Module.
- Existing platform adapter method names and signatures remain compatible.
- Tests cover routing outcomes for at least Telegram, a generic platform, and one platform with known media quirks.
- Regression coverage includes a background/kanban artifact delivery path and a cron `MEDIA:` delivery path.

### Recommendation strength
Strong.

This is a strong deepening opportunity because the existing bug surface already shows media routing drift across gateway delivery paths, while the proposed Module can provide high leverage behind a small Interface without reopening any documented ADR decision.

items.body:
# Add `register_tts_provider()` plugin hook for Python-SDK and streaming TTS engines

## Summary

Add a `TTSProvider(ABC)` + `register_tts_provider()` extension point to the plugin context API, **alongside** the existing config-driven `tts.providers.<name>: type: command` registry from #17843. This is **additive, not a replacement** — the command-provider surface stays as the primary way to add a TTS backend.

The hook covers cases the shell-template grammar can't reasonably express:

- Native Python SDKs without a CLI (Cartesia, Fish Audio, modern startups)
- Streaming synthesis (chunked Opus → Telegram voice-bubble while text generates)
- Voice metadata API for the `hermes tools` picker (`provider.list_voices()`)
- OAuth-refreshing auth (no equivalent in shell-template flow)

This issue does **not** propose porting any of the 10 inline built-in providers (`edge`, `openai`, `elevenlabs`, `minimax`, `gemini`, `mistral`, `xai`, `piper`, `kittentts`, `neutts`) to plugins. They stay inline. The hook is for *new* engines.

## Current state

**Two existing TTS extension surfaces** (both established by Teknium):

1. **Built-in providers** (`BUILTIN_TTS_PROVIDERS` frozenset in `tools/tts_tool.py:339`) — 10 inline backends with native Python SDK calls. Surfaced as hardcoded rows in `TOOL_CATEGORIES["tts"]["providers"]` (`hermes_cli/tools_config.py:199-273`).

2. **Command-provider registry** — `tts.providers.<name>: type: command` (PR #17843, commit `2facea7f7`). Lets users wire any local or external TTS CLI into Hermes without Python. Placeholder grammar covers `{input_path}`, `{output_path}`, `{format}`, `{voice}`, `{model}`, `{speed}`. Shell-quote-aware. 42 tests in `tests/tools/test_tts_command_providers.py`.

Built-in names always win over `tts.providers.<name>` collisions — established precedence rule.

**What's missing:** A third path for backends that are NOT a single shell command. Specifically:

- A vendor ships a Python SDK only (no CLI) → user has to write `python -c "..."` one-liner in `tts.providers.<name>.command`, losing voice listing, streaming, and Python-object kwargs.
- A backend needs streaming bytes for live voice-bubble assembly → command providers flush only on subprocess exit, breaking streaming.
- A community plugin wants to add a TTS engine alongside its other functionality (e.g. a Spotify plugin that exposes a TTS for read-aloud) → no plugin hook.

Doc commit `a401f8172` (Teknium) flagged this explicitly:

> "Future `register_tts_provider()`/`register_stt_provider()` hooks mentioned as nice-to-have for SDK/streaming cases, not as the primary story."

This issue captures the design so a contributor can pick it up.

## Why this hook (and not a full plugin migration)

| | Full migration of built-ins | This hook |
|---|---|---|
| Touches built-in code | Yes — refactors 10 backends | No — built-ins untouched |
| Replaces `tts.providers.<name>: type: command` | Effectively (overlap UX) | No — coexists, command wins on collision |
| Risk to existing users | High — 10 backends to test parity | Low — opt-in only when plugin registers a new name |
| Net LoC | Probably +0/-0 (structural move) | ~+500 net (additive surface) |
| Teknium's stated preference | Against (per `a401f8172`) | Aligned with stated "nice-to-have" |

The hook is the responsible incremental step. A full migration would be its own future debate.

## Resolution order (extended)

The dispatcher's resolution order is the load-bearing invariant. After this change:

1. **`tts.provider` is a built-in name** (`edge`, `openai`, `elevenlabs`, etc.) → built-in dispatch. **Always wins.**
2. **`tts.provider` matches `tts.providers.<name>` with `command:` set** → command-provider dispatch (config-driven, PR #17843).
3. **`tts.provider` matches a plugin-registered `TTSProvider`** → plugin dispatch (new).
4. **No match** → error: "provider not found".

This preserves both pre-existing rules:
- Built-ins-always-win (built-in plugin name shadowing rejected at registration time)
- Command-provider name registered in `config.yaml` wins over a same-name plugin (config is more local than plugin install)

## Architecture

### New files

**`agent/tts_provider.py`** (~120 LoC) — Public ABC. Mirrors `agent/image_gen_provider.py` / `agent/video_gen_provider.py` shape:

```python
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List, Optional


class TTSProvider(ABC):
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def name(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def display_name(self) -> str: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def is_available(self) -> bool: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def synthesize(
        self,
        text: str,
        output_path: str,
        *,
        voice: Optional[str] = None,
        model: Optional[str] = None,
        speed: Optional[float] = None,
        format: str = "mp3",
        **extra: Any,
    ) -> str:
        """Write audio to output_path, return path."""

    # Optional hooks (default no-op):
    def list_voices(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: return []
    def list_models(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: return []
    def get_setup_schema(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {"name": self.display_name, "env_vars": []}

    def stream(self, text: str, *, voice=None, model=None, format="opus", **extra) -> Iterator[bytes]:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"{self.name} does not support streaming")

    @property
    def voice_compatible(self) -> bool: return False
```

**`agent/tts_registry.py`** (~60 LoC) — Standard registry: `register_provider`, `get_provider`, `list_providers`. Registration rejects names in `BUILTIN_TTS_PROVIDERS` with a warning (built-ins-always-win invariant).

### Modified files

**`hermes_cli/plugins.py`** — Add `register_tts_provider()` to `PluginContext`. Same shape as `register_image_gen_provider()` (lines 531-554):

```python
def register_tts_provider(self, provider) -> None:
    from agent.tts_provider import TTSProvider
    from agent.tts_registry import register_provider

    if not isinstance(provider, TTSProvider):
        logger.warning(
            "Plugin '%s' tried to register a TTS provider that does "
            "not inherit from TTSProvider. Ignoring.",
            self.manifest.name,
        )
        return
    register_provider(provider)
    logger.info(
        "Plugin '%s' registered TTS provider: %s",
        self.manifest.name, provider.name,
    )
```

**`tools/tts_tool.py`** — Add `_dispatch_to_plugin_provider()` and call it from `text_to_speech_tool()` BEFORE the command-provider check is reached for non-built-in names. Single insertion point in the existing `_get_provider()` → dispatch flow. No built-in code paths touched.

```python
def _dispatch_to_plugin_provider(
    text: str, output_path: str, tts_config: Dict[str, Any]
) -> Optional[str]:
    name = _get_provider(tts_config)
    # Built-ins always win
    if name in BUILTIN_TTS_PROVIDERS:
        return None
    # Command provider wins over plugin on same name
    if _get_provider_section(tts_config, name).get("command"):
        return None

    try:
        from agent.tts_registry import get_provider
        from hermes_cli.plugins import _ensure_plugins_discovered
        _ensure_plugins_discovered()
        provider = get_provider(name)
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.debug("tts plugin dispatch skipped: %s", exc)
        return None

    if provider is None:
        return None

    voice = tts_config.get("voice")
    model = tts_config.get("model")
    speed = tts_config.get("speed")
    fmt = tts_config.get("output_format", "mp3")
    return provider.synthesize(text, output_path, voice=voice, model=model, speed=speed, format=fmt)
```

**`hermes_cli/tools_config.py`** — Add `_plugin_tts_providers()` mirroring `_plugin_image_gen_providers()` (line 1507-area on current main). Surfaces plugin-registered TTS providers in the `hermes tools` picker. Pulls each plugin's `get_setup_schema()` for env_vars + tag + badge. Skips any plugin name in `BUILTIN_TTS_PROVIDERS` (defensive — registration already blocks this).

### Docs

**`website/docs/user-guide/features/tts.md`** — Add a new section after the existing "Custom command providers" section explaining when to pick which:

| Backend has… | Use |
|---|---|
| A single CLI that reads stdin/file and writes stdout/file | `tts.providers.<name>: type: command` |
| A Python SDK only (no CLI) | `register_tts_provider()` plugin |
| Streaming bytes you want to deliver mid-generation | `register_tts_provider()` plugin with `stream()` |
| A voice-listing API used by `hermes setup` | `register_tts_provider()` plugin with `list_voices()` |

Plus a minimal "Hello World" plugin example mirroring the image-gen plugin example in `build-a-hermes-plugin.md`.

## Atomic PR breakdown

Each PR is self-contained, self-verifiable, lands behavior-neutral until the last one, and ships independently usable on its own. None of them depend on any later PR landing first.

### PR 1 — `agent/tts_provider.py` + `agent/tts_registry.py` foundation

**Scope:** Add the ABC and registry. No callers. No dispatch wiring. No plugin hook.

**Why this is self-contained:** Standalone module. No effect on production code paths — nothing imports `tts_provider`/`tts_registry` until PR 3. Tests cover the registry in isolation (registration, get/list, built-in shadow rejection).

**Files:**
- `agent/tts_provider.py` (new, ~120 LoC)
- `agent/tts_registry.py` (new, ~60 LoC)
- `tests/agent/test_tts_registry.py` (new, ~80 LoC)

**Verification:**
- `pytest tests/agent/test_tts_registry.py` — covers: register, register-twice-replaces, register-builtin-rejected, get-missing-returns-None, list-returns-frozen-copy.
- Existing TTS tests (`tests/tools/test_tts*.py`) untouched, all pass.
- No diff in `tools/tts_tool.py`, `hermes_cli/plugins.py`, or `hermes_cli/tools_config.py`.

**Acceptance:** `grep -r "tts_registry\|tts_provider" tools/ hermes_cli/` returns nothing — proves the foundation is genuinely dormant until later PRs wire it in.

### PR 2 — `register_tts_provider()` PluginContext hook

**Scope:** Add the registration entry point. Built-ins-rejection is enforced HERE (registry path is also defensive, but most callers go through the context hook).

**Why this is self-contained:** Adds a method to `PluginContext` that any plugin can call, but no plugin yet uses it AND the dispatcher doesn't yet read the registry. Plugins that try to call it just register into a registry no one reads — observable as a log line but no behavior change.

**Files:**
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py` (+30 LoC) — `register_tts_provider()` method
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_tts_registration.py` (new, ~60 LoC)

**Verification:**
- Test: a fake plugin calling `ctx.register_tts_provider(FakeProvider())` ends up in the registry.
- Test: a fake plugin calling `ctx.register_tts_provider(NotATTSProvider())` is rejected with a warning, registry stays empty.
- Test: a fake plugin trying to register with `name = "edge"` is rejected (built-in shadow).
- `tools/tts_tool.py` unchanged. All existing TTS tests pass.

**Acceptance:** A test plugin that registers a TTSProvider gets into `list_providers()` — but generating speech via `text_to_speech_tool` still ignores the registry (proven by another test asserting the legacy path is taken). This pins down the "PR is dormant" promise.

### PR 3 — Dispatcher cutover in `tools/tts_tool.py`

**Scope:** Wire `_dispatch_to_plugin_provider()` into the TTS flow. After this PR, `tts.provider: my-cartesia` (a plugin name) actually routes to the plugin.

**Why this is self-contained:** The wiring is one insertion point. Behavior change is *only* observable for users who already installed a TTS plugin (zero today, since no plugins exist before this issue). For everyone else, the dispatcher resolution order is identical to today: built-ins-then-command-providers-then-error.

**Files:**
- `tools/tts_tool.py` (+40 LoC) — `_dispatch_to_plugin_provider()` + entry-point call
- `tests/tools/test_tts_plugin_dispatch.py` (new, ~150 LoC)
- `tests/tools/test_tts_command_providers.py` — verify pass-through, no test modifications expected
- `tests/plugins/tts/check_parity_vs_main.py` (new, ~200 LoC) — subprocess parity harness

**Verification:**
- 6 parity scenarios via subprocess harness:
  1. `unset` → both: built-in edge (default)
  2. `tts.provider: openai` → both: built-in openai (built-in wins)
  3. `tts.provider: my-cli` + `tts.providers.my-cli.command: ...` → both: command-provider (command wins)
  4. `tts.provider: cartesia` (no plugin, no command) → both: error "provider not found"
  5. `tts.provider: cartesia` + plugin installed → main: error, PR: plugin dispatch (only intentional diff)
  6. `tts.provider: edge` + plugin tries to register name `edge` → both: built-in edge, registry rejects plugin

  All non-diff scenarios are `[OK]`; scenario 5 is `[DIFF] legacy_error → plugin_dispatch — expected`.

- Unit tests:
  - Plugin dispatches when name is not built-in, not command-provider, AND registry has it
  - Plugin does NOT dispatch when name is built-in (built-in wins)
  - Plugin does NOT dispatch when same-name command provider is configured (command wins)
  - Plugin dispatch exception → graceful error JSON (matches command-provider exception shape)

- All 130+ existing TTS tests pass. `tests/tools/test_tts_command_providers.py` specifically asserts the command-provider precedence didn't change.

**Acceptance:** Parity harness exits 0. Built-ins-always-win invariant + command-wins-over-plugin invariant both have dedicated tests with explicit assertion comments referencing PR #17843.

### PR 4 — `hermes tools` picker surface

**Scope:** Plugin TTS providers show up in `hermes tools` like image-gen plugins do today (post-FAL-migration). Picker reads `get_setup_schema()` and injects rows.

**Why this is self-contained:** Picker-only. Doesn't touch dispatch. No effect on runtime synthesis. Only visible when (a) a TTS plugin is installed and (b) the user opens the picker. Existing built-in rows in `TOOL_CATEGORIES["tts"]["providers"]` stay as-is — no rewrite.

**Files:**
- `hermes_cli/tools_config.py` (+50 LoC) — `_plugin_tts_providers()` + call site in `_visible_providers`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_tts_picker.py` (+ assertions, ~40 LoC of new tests)

**Verification:**
- Test: with no TTS plugins, picker shows exactly the existing hardcoded rows (no change).
- Test: with one TTS plugin registered (e.g. fake "cartesia"), picker shows the existing rows + a Cartesia row at the bottom.
- Test: plugin row carries `tts_provider: <name>` so writing config selects it correctly.
- Test: a plugin with `name="edge"` is filtered out of the picker (defense against builtin-shadow plugin slipping through registration).

**Acceptance:** `hermes tools` UX is unchanged for users with no TTS plugins installed.

### PR 5 — Docs + reference plugin example

**Scope:** Update `website/docs/user-guide/features/tts.md` with the "command vs plugin" decision table + a minimal "hello world" TTS plugin example. Update `build-a-hermes-plugin.md` to mention `register_tts_provider()` alongside the other register hooks.

**Why this is self-contained:** Docs-only. Zero code change. Safe to merge anytime after PR 1 lands.

**Files:**
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/tts.md` (+~80 LoC new section)
- `website/docs/contributing/build-a-hermes-plugin.md` (+~30 LoC TTS row + example)
- `website/docs/contributing/plugins.md` (+~5 LoC — TTS row update: from "Config-driven (not a Python plugin)" → "Config-driven (command-providers) OR Python plugin via `register_tts_provider()` — see [tts.md](...)")

**Verification:**
- `cd website && npx docusaurus build` — zero broken links, builds clean.
- Manual: anchors `#custom-command-providers`, `#plugin-providers` both resolve.
- Live URL check: `curl -sI https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/tts` returns 200 (or it's not deployed yet — verify against the live URL after merge).

**Acceptance:** Doc-only diff. No code touched.

### PR 6 (optional, AFTER a consumer shows up) — Reference plugin

**Scope:** Ship ONE reference plugin to validate the surface. **Do not file this PR speculatively.** File it only when a real contributor wants to upstream a Cartesia / Fish Audio / similar Python-SDK TTS engine. The reference plugin proves the surface holds up to a real implementation.

**Why this is separate:** Filing reference plugins without a real consumer creates dead code. Per the skill's "Plugin (for third-party/niche capabilities)" guidance, plugins should land when they're actually needed.

## Out of scope

- **Porting any built-in (`edge`, `openai`, `elevenlabs`, `minimax`, `gemini`, `mistral`, `xai`, `piper`, `kittentts`, `neutts`) to a plugin.** They stay inline. This is the bright line that distinguishes this issue from a full migration.
- **Deprecating `tts.providers.<name>: type: command`.** Both paths coexist. The command-provider registry remains the primary recommendation for "I have a CLI" cases.
- **Implementing streaming-Opus for existing built-ins.** `stream()` is on the ABC for new providers; built-ins keep using `synthesize()`.
- **`register_stt_provider()` for transcription.** Separate concern, separate issue. The transcription migration to plugins is the better foundation for STT pluggability.
- **Voice-bubble delivery refactor.** `voice_compatible` is exposed on the ABC matching the `tts.providers.<name>.voice_compatible` field; existing voice-bubble logic (`tools/tts_tool.py::_should_deliver_as_voice_bubble`) is not refactored here.

## Acceptance criteria for the whole issue

After all 5 PRs land:

1. A Python developer can ship a plugin at `plugins/my-tts-engine/` that calls `ctx.register_tts_provider(MyProvider())` and have it work end-to-end (config select → synthesize → audio file delivered).
2. Existing users on `tts.provider: edge` / `openai` / etc. see zero behavior change.
3. Existing users on `tts.providers.<name>: type: command` see zero behavior change.
4. A plugin attempting to shadow `edge` (or any built-in) is rejected with a warning, and the built-in still works.
5. `hermes tools` surfaces installed TTS plugins as picker rows.
6. Docs explain when to pick command-provider vs plugin.
7. `tests/tools/test_tts*.py` all pass with no modifications (existing tests prove no regression).

## Pre-flight checklist for the contributor

Before writing code:
- [ ] Read PR #17843 (command-provider registry) — the surface this hook coexists with.
- [ ] Read PR #25214 (browser plugin migration) — the architectural template.
- [ ] Read PR #30380 (FAL image-gen plugin migration) — the most recent reference, includes the parity-harness pattern.
- [ ] Read commit `a401f8172` — Teknium's correction on what TTS pluggability means today.
- [ ] Read `references/plugin-extraction-test-patch-compatibility.md` rules in the `hermes-agent-dev` skill if you go anywhere near built-in code (you shouldn't have to — built-ins stay inline).

## Related

- PR #17843 (`feat(tts): add command-type provider registry under tts.providers.<name>`) — the existing extension surface.
- Commit `a401f8172` — Teknium's "they ARE plugins via command-providers" doc correction, mentions `register_tts_provider()` as a future nice-to-have.
- PR #30380 — FAL image-gen plugin migration (architectural template, just landed May 22 2026).
- PR #25214 — browser plugin migration (closest analog for net-new plugin context API).
- #26241 — FAL migration issue, structurally similar to this one (different conclusion: that one migrated everything, this one is additive).

items.title: Hermes should stop repeated tool loops and block obviously broken final responses

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## What happened

Hermes let a model get stuck, call tools repeatedly, then send a huge broken final answer to Telegram as if it were a normal reply.

The important detail is that the provider returned:

```text
finish_reason=stop
```

So Hermes treated the output as a clean final answer, not as a truncation or model error.

This happened twice in the same incident.

## Why this matters

When an agent gets stuck, the user should get a short controlled failure message, not a 70k-150k character blob.

This also matters because once Hermes saves the broken answer as normal assistant output, downstream memory systems can ingest it as if it were useful context.

That is exactly what happened here.

## Sanitized environment

```text
platform: Telegram
model: kimi-k2.6
session: sess_a19a949215
session_end_reason: compression
message_count: 182
```

Raw Telegram IDs, raw session IDs, secrets, and message contents are omitted.

## Diagnostic data

### First bad final answer

```text
message_id: 6853
session: sess_a19a949215
role: assistant
finish_reason: stop
chars: 149,795
count("I'll"): 7,568
count("Let me"): 29
```

Before that answer, Hermes had already allowed a repeated terminal loop:

```text
message rows: 6822-6852
tool: terminal
repeated tool outputs: 16
each repeated output length: 564 chars
```

Plain English: the model kept doing effectively the same kind of lookup, got effectively the same result, and Hermes let it keep going.

### Second bad final answer

```text
message_id: 7043
session: sess_a19a949215
role: assistant
finish_reason: stop
chars: 70,672
count("I'll"): 3,945
count("Let me"): 7
```

Before that answer, the model had been repeatedly using browser/docs tools:

```text
browser_navigate: 11
browser_console: 7
browser_click: 7
browser_vision: 2
browser_snapshot: 2
web_extract: 1
```

Again, Hermes treated the final output as normal because the provider said `finish_reason=stop`.

## What I expected Hermes to do

Hermes should catch two things before sending a reply to the user:

1. repeated no-progress tool use;
2. obviously broken final output.

The final output check should run even when `finish_reason=stop`.

## Suggested fix

### 1. Stop repeated no-progress tool loops

Hermes should detect patterns like:

```text
same tool + same/similar args + same/similar result, repeated N times in one turn
```

This should include successful tool calls, not just failed ones.

A terminal command can succeed and still make no progress.

When this triggers, Hermes should stop the run and return a short message like:

```text
I got stuck repeating the same lookup and stopped before sending a bad answer.
```

### 2. Check final answers before gateway delivery

Before saving and sending a final assistant response, Hermes should check for:

```text
extreme length
very high repetition
thousands of repeated phrase starts
self-drafting text
obvious loop text
platform-specific delivery limits
```

If the response looks broken, Hermes should not send the raw body to Telegram.

Possible recovery:

1. retry once with a repair prompt asking for a short final answer only; or
2. send a safe abort message and store metadata about what was suppressed.

## What should be tested

Please add regression tests for:

1. repeated successful terminal calls with the same result trigger a hard stop;
2. a `finish_reason=stop` answer over 70k chars with high repetition is blocked;
3. the gateway does not send the full broken body;
4. the session store records that a guardrail fired;
5. context engines / memory providers do not receive the raw broken body as normal assistant text;
6. legitimate long reports are not blocked just because they are long.

## Related work

This is related to tool-loop guardrails and length recovery, but it is not the same as truncation recovery.

The bad responses here were not `finish_reason=length`.

They were:

```text
finish_reason=stop
```

So Hermes needs a separate "does this final answer look sane?" guard.

items.title: [Bug]: Telegram DM auto-topic-rename and tool-call routing broken by _recover_telegram_topic_thread_id()

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description

Root-DM messages to the Hermes Telegram gateway no longer create new topics. Every reply from the root DM gets pinned back to whatever topic you were most recently talking in. Auto-topic-renaming also silently breaks when `disable_topic_auto_rename` is not explicitly set.

Previously, sending a new message from the root Telegram DM created a new topic, got auto-renamed to match the conversation after a turn, and had tool-call progress routed to that same topic. Now new root messages silently re-use the last active topic, breaking session isolation — you end up with two separate conversations tangled in one topic, or tool-call output showing up in a different topic than where you replied.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes gateway with Telegram enabled, `telegram.extra.disable_topic_auto_rename` unset (defaults to `false`).
2. Send a message from the Telegram root DM — a new topic is created (expected).
3. Reply in that topic — it gets auto-renamed (may or may not work depending on flag state).
4. Send a *new* message from the root DM again — instead of creating a fresh topic, the response appears in the topic from step 2.

### Expected Behavior

A new root-DM message creates a new topic. After one turn in the new topic, the topic gets auto-renamed to match the conversation. Tool-call progress routes to whichever topic the conversation is in.

### Actual Behavior

Root-DM messages no longer create new topics. Instead, `_recover_telegram_topic_thread_id()` pins them to the most recent topic, which breaks the expected root-DM → new-topic flow and makes auto-rename/tool-call routing behave incorrectly. 

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

```shell
Unable to run `hermes debug share` at time of filing. Root cause is identified below with file paths and code references.
```

### Operating System

CachyOS (Arch-based)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v2026.5.16-702-ga8cbcf1c8

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The bug is in `gateway/run.py`. Commit `ede47a54b` added `_recover_telegram_topic_thread_id()` which routes incoming root-DM messages to the user's most recent topic instead of creating a new one. The revert is straightforward — `git revert ede47a54b`.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Revert commit `ede47a54b`. If the pinning behavior (routing root-DM replies to the current topic) is desired, make it opt-in via a config flag like `telegram.extra.pin_root_dm_replies: true`.

items.title: [Bug]: terminal.docker_extra_args silently ignored in gateway mode (missing env-var bridge)
items.body:
### Bug Description

\`config.yaml\`'s \`terminal.docker_extra_args\` is silently dropped when the gateway spawns per-session sandbox containers, because \`gateway/run.py\`'s \`_terminal_env_map\` (which bridges \`terminal.*\` config keys into \`TERMINAL_*\` env vars at module import time) omits \`docker_extra_args\` from the map. Every other \`terminal.*\` key in that block IS bridged, so users reasonably expect this one to be too.

Net effect: sandbox containers spawn without any of the documented extra args (extra bind mounts, devices, capabilities, etc.). The agent's file tools — which run inside that sandbox under \`terminal.backend: docker\` — then can't see the paths the user mounted via \`docker_extra_args\`, and the failure surfaces as \`{\"error\": \"Path not found\"}\` from \`search_files\` / \`read_file\` against the missing mount. The model often improvises by writing to \`/tmp/...\` inside the sandbox, where nobody ever sees the output.

### Repro

\`config.yaml\`:
\`\`\`yaml
terminal:
  backend: docker
  docker_extra_args:
    - -v=/home/me/notes:/opt/notes
\`\`\`

Then run via the gateway (any messaging platform) and have the agent try to list \`/opt/notes\`:

- \`search_files\` with \`path: \"/opt/notes\"\` → \`Path not found: /opt/notes\`
- \`terminal\` with \`ls /opt/notes\` → \`No such file or directory\`
- \`docker inspect <spawned-sandbox> --format '{{.HostConfig.Binds}}'\` shows no \`/opt/notes\` mount.

### Diagnosis

Inside the gateway container the env var is unset:
\`\`\`
$ docker exec <gateway> printenv TERMINAL_DOCKER_EXTRA_ARGS
(empty)
\`\`\`

\`tools/terminal_tool.py:1093\`:
\`\`\`python
\"docker_extra_args\": _parse_env_var(\"TERMINAL_DOCKER_EXTRA_ARGS\", \"[]\", json.loads, \"valid JSON\"),
\`\`\`

So \`_get_env_config()\` reads the env var (unset → \`[]\`) and the value from \`config.yaml\` never makes it through.

\`gateway/run.py:443-468\` does bridge most other \`terminal.*\` keys:
\`\`\`python
_terminal_env_map = {
    \"backend\": \"TERMINAL_ENV\",
    \"cwd\": \"TERMINAL_CWD\",
    \"timeout\": \"TERMINAL_TIMEOUT\",
    \"lifetime_seconds\": \"TERMINAL_LIFETIME_SECONDS\",
    \"docker_image\": \"TERMINAL_DOCKER_IMAGE\",
    \"docker_forward_env\": \"TERMINAL_DOCKER_FORWARD_ENV\",
    # … singularity_image, modal_image, daytona_image, vercel_runtime, ssh_*,
    # container_cpu, container_memory, container_disk, container_persistent,
    \"docker_volumes\": \"TERMINAL_DOCKER_VOLUMES\",
    \"docker_env\": \"TERMINAL_DOCKER_ENV\",
    \"docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace\": \"TERMINAL_DOCKER_MOUNT_CWD_TO_WORKSPACE\",
    \"docker_run_as_host_user\": \"TERMINAL_DOCKER_RUN_AS_HOST_USER\",
    \"sandbox_dir\": \"TERMINAL_SANDBOX_DIR\",
    \"persistent_shell\": \"TERMINAL_PERSISTENT_SHELL\",
}
\`\`\`

\`docker_extra_args\` is the only \`terminal.docker_*\` setting in that file that's absent.

### Expected vs Actual

- **Expected**: \`config.yaml\`'s \`terminal.docker_extra_args\` reaches the sandbox spawn via the same path as \`docker_volumes\` / \`docker_env\` / \`docker_image\`. (The CLI path reads the config directly so this works in CLI mode — only gateway-spawned sessions miss it.)
- **Actual**: silently ignored in gateway mode. No warning, no log line.

### Proposed Fix

One line in \`gateway/run.py\`'s \`_terminal_env_map\`, alongside the other docker_* entries. Need to JSON-encode the value before exporting (mirroring how the matching code does it for \`docker_volumes\` / \`docker_env\`, which are also list/dict types):

\`\`\`python
\"docker_extra_args\": \"TERMINAL_DOCKER_EXTRA_ARGS\",
\`\`\`

The existing block at \`run.py:482-485\` already handles list/dict serialization for the bridged values:
\`\`\`python
if isinstance(_val, (list, dict)):
    os.environ[_env_var] = json.dumps(_val)
else:
    os.environ[_env_var] = str(_val)
\`\`\`
so no additional encoding logic needed — just the missing map entry.

### Workaround (until upstream patches it)

Set the env var directly in the gateway's container env, JSON-encoded:

\`\`\`yaml
services:
  gateway:
    environment:
      - TERMINAL_DOCKER_EXTRA_ARGS=[\"-v=/home/me/notes:/opt/notes\"]
\`\`\`

We hit this debugging a separate gosu/group-add issue (#16703 — comment posted today). Both bugs together produce a particularly confusing UX in messaging-platform mode: the file tools that ARE in the schema can't see the paths the user mounted, and the model rationalizes the failures into a story about platform sandboxing.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes — happy to send the one-line PR if it'd help.

The CLI mode has a beautiful animated spinner (`⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏`) with kawaii faces during API thinking/tool calls, but the TUI (Ink) mode only shows static text like `(◔_◔) pondering...` without any animation.

- `KawaiiSpinner` in `agent/display.py` cycles through braille frames via `\r` overwrites
- Shows animated: `⠹ (◔_◔) pondering...` (spinner rotates)

1. Detects when status is a "thinking" state (e.g., contains thinking verbs like "pondering", "contemplating", etc.)

3. Prepends the animated frame to the status text

items.title: Add Bedrock image generation provider (Stability AI)

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Hermes already supports AWS Bedrock for inference (`plugins/model-providers/bedrock/`). Users running Claude on Bedrock have a working `bedrock-runtime` client and AWS credentials configured (env vars / `AWS_PROFILE` / IRSA / IMDS / `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`). They cannot generate images today without bringing in a separate vendor (OpenAI / xAI / FAL / Nous Portal), even though the same Bedrock account natively offers Stability AI text-to-image models in `us-west-2` (`stability.sd3-5-large-v1:0`, `stability.stable-image-core-v1:1`, `stability.stable-image-ultra-v1:1`).

**Concrete trigger.** A non-technical family member running this agent hit `image_generate` and got a hard failure because none of `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `XAI_API_KEY` / `FAL_KEY` / Nous Portal were set, despite chat working fine through Bedrock. Adding any of those means a second billing relationship and a second key to manage for a capability the existing AWS account already covers — particularly painful for AWS-only shops where adding a vendor needs procurement / security review.

**Why Stability and not Amazon Nova Canvas.** I originally scoped this for `amazon.nova-canvas-v1:0`, but verified before opening the PR that AWS has marked Nova Canvas (and Titan Image G1 v2) as `LEGACY` in every region that offers them (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-northeast-1`), with `endOfLifeTime: 2026-09-30` per `aws bedrock get-foundation-model`. New invocations from accounts that haven't called the model in the prior 30 days return `ResourceNotFoundException: This Model is marked by provider as Legacy and you have not been actively using the model`. Shipping a Nova Canvas plugin would be a 4-month liability. Stability AI text-to-image models in `us-west-2` are `ACTIVE` with no announced deprecation — `stable-image-ultra-v1:1` was smoke-tested via `bedrock-runtime invoke_model` and returned a usable PNG.

**Why this isn't a skill.** Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#should-it-be-a-skill-or-a-tool): "Most capabilities should be skills, not tools." This proposal is neither. It's a new **backend for an existing tool's plugin registry** — `image_gen` already has the pluggable architecture (`agent.image_gen_registry`, `agent.image_gen_provider.ImageGenProvider` ABC), and every existing backend lives as a separate plugin directory: `plugins/image_gen/openai/`, `plugins/image_gen/openai-codex/`, `plugins/image_gen/xai/`, `plugins/image_gen/fal/`. This proposal slots into that established structure, mirroring #14317 (`openai-codex`) and #14765 (`xai`) — no new tool, no new top-level architecture, just one more entry in an existing registry.

A `terminal`-driven skill calling `aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model` was considered but rejected: the agent harness handles base64-PNG persistence, cache directory routing, aspect-ratio resolution, and provider-availability gating uniformly via the `ImageGenProvider` ABC. Bypassing that would mean re-implementing those affordances per skill invocation and breaking the `hermes tools` provider picker.

### Proposed Solution

New plugin at `plugins/image_gen/bedrock-stability/` following the precedent set by #13799 (image_gen plugin architecture + OpenAI provider), #14317 (`openai-codex`), and #14765 (`xai`).

**Surface area:**
- One new plugin directory: `plugins/image_gen/bedrock-stability/{plugin.yaml, __init__.py}`
- One new test file: `tests/plugins/image_gen/test_bedrock_stability_provider.py`
- **Zero new third-party dependencies** — boto3 is already declared in the `provider.bedrock` group in `pyproject.toml` (used by the inference plugin); the new plugin reuses the same `tools.lazy_deps.ensure("provider.bedrock")` hook
- **Zero changes to `cli-config.yaml.example`** — consistent with how existing image_gen plugins (`openai`, `xai`, `fal`) handle their `image_gen.<provider>.*` keys today (none are listed in the example file)
- **Zero changes to core code** — no edits to `agent/`, `tools/`, `hermes_cli/`, or `pyproject.toml`. The plugin self-registers via `register(ctx)` like every other image_gen backend.

**Behavior:**
- Provider name `bedrock-stability` (leaves namespace open for sibling `bedrock-titan` / `bedrock-nova` plugins later if AWS launches non-legacy successors — same precedent as `openai` vs `openai-codex`)
- Catalog (all currently `ACTIVE` text-to-image in `us-west-2` per `aws bedrock list-foundation-models`):
  - `stability.sd3-5-large-v1:0` — flagship, set as `default_model`
  - `stability.stable-image-core-v1:1` — fast tier
  - `stability.stable-image-ultra-v1:1` — highest quality
- Calls `bedrock-runtime.invoke_model` with the [documented Stability schema](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-stability-diffusion.html); response `images[0]` (base64 PNG) is persisted via `agent.image_gen_provider.save_b64_image` to `$HERMES_HOME/cache/images/`
- Auth: reuses `agent.bedrock_adapter.has_aws_credentials` for `is_available()` gating and `_get_bedrock_runtime_client(region)` for the cached boto3 client — anything boto3's credential chain accepts works without new prompts in `hermes setup`
- Aspect ratios: passed via the Stability `aspect_ratio` field (`"16:9"`, `"1:1"`, `"9:16"`) — Stability returns appropriate dimensions natively, no manual width/height math
- Region precedence: `image_gen.bedrock-stability.region` → `bedrock.region` → `agent.bedrock_adapter.resolve_bedrock_region()` (covers `AWS_REGION` / `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` / botocore session) → **`us-west-2` fallback** (where the models are actually `ACTIVE`; differs from inference-plugin default of `us-east-1` because Stability text-to-image isn't offered in `us-east-1`)

**Security posture:**
- User prompts are passed as JSON string fields to `boto3.invoke_model`, never spliced into shell commands, file paths, or `eval`
- No new credential surface — `get_setup_schema()` returns `env_vars=[]` deliberately, so `hermes setup` won't write AWS access keys to `~/.hermes/.env` and clobber users' existing `~/.aws/credentials` or SSO sessions

**Cross-platform:**
- All I/O goes through existing helpers (`save_b64_image`, `_get_bedrock_runtime_client`); no new platform-specific path handling
- boto3 is officially supported on macOS, Linux, and Windows/WSL2

### Alternatives Considered

1. **A bare `bedrock` provider that fans out to all Bedrock image models under one router.** Rejected — each model family has a distinct request schema and pricing profile. Hiding which one is being billed contradicts the `openai` vs `openai-codex` precedent that separate auth/billing surfaces deserve separate plugins even within one vendor.
2. **Ship Nova Canvas anyway and follow up when EOL hits.** Rejected — Nova Canvas is `LEGACY` in every region today, with a 30-day inactivity block already enforced and a hard cutoff in 2026-09-30. Merging a plugin that will need to be ripped out in 4 months is worse than skipping it.
3. **Document a `comfyui`-skill route on a self-hosted GPU box.** Overkill for users who just want "decent text-to-image from a prompt"; Stability on Bedrock covers that with managed infra and pay-per-use billing already attached to the existing AWS account.
4. **Wait for Nous Portal to bundle Bedrock.** No public timeline, and the AWS-only-shop case stays unsolved (Nous Portal is itself a separate billing relationship).
5. **Tell users to set `FAL_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` instead.** Works technically; defeats the point of running on Bedrock to begin with.

### Feature Type

New tool

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Kanban DB corruption risk from multi-gateway concurrent SQLite access
items.body:
## Description
Every Hermes profile gateway opens a SQLite connection to the shared kanban.db on startup, regardless of whether the profile has `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway` enabled. On a multi-profile setup with 7+ active gateways, this creates 7+ concurrent SQLite connections to the same WAL-mode database.

## Root Cause
When one process runs `hermes kanban init` (which deletes and recreates the file), older gateway processes hold file handles on the old inode. New processes write to the new inode, while old processes may still write to the stale inode, causing `database disk image is malformed` and `disk I/O error`.

lsof output from a typical setup:
```
7 python processes × ~40 file descriptors each = 280+ open handles on kanban.db
```

## Suggested Fixes (any would help)
1. Gateways with `dispatch_in_gateway: false` should skip kanban DB initialization entirely
2. Add a per-profile config flag like `kanban.enabled: false` to prevent DB connection on non-participating profiles
3. Single-writer proxy: only one process (the architect gateway) writes to SQLite; other gateways communicate via IPC

## Workaround Deployed
We wrote a cron-based health checker (`kanban_health.py`) that runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` every 6 hours, kills zombie processes holding stale handles, runs `hermes kanban init`, and restarts all gateways. This is a band-aid, not a proper fix.

## Environment
- Profiles: architect (dispatch=true), wikid (dispatch=true), a-dev, a-creative, a-eval, a-view, intel-pilot (dispatch=false but still open handles)
- All gateways running on same Linux host, same user

items.title: Bug: Session-only /model overrides are silently lost on Telegram Group Forum threads and during Session Splits (Context Compression)
items.body:
### Describe the Bug
There are two critical leaks in `gateway/run.py` where active, session-only `/model` overrides are silently discarded or bypassed, causing the agent to fall back to the global `config.yaml` default without warning the user.

---

### Bug 1: Telegram Group Forum Topic (Thread ID Suffix) Callback Mismatch

In Telegram groups with multiple forum topics enabled, the gateway isolates sessions by appending `:thread_id` to the session key (e.g., `agent:main:telegram:group:-100123456789:1`).

1. **How it fails:**
   When a user invokes `/model` and clicks a model button from the inline keyboard, the callback query handling inside `_on_model_selected` builds the `_session_key` from the callback message. Depending on the Telegram payload, the `message_thread_id` can be lost, causing the override to be saved under the *base group session key* (without the `:thread_id` suffix):
   - Override Saved: `agent:main:telegram:group:-100123456789`

2. **The Mismatch:**
   Subsequent messages sent by the user inside the specific forum topic topic route through the *thread session key*:
   - Message Route: `agent:main:telegram:group:-100123456789:1`

   Because `_apply_session_model_override` performs a straight dictionary lookup using the current message's `session_key`, it fails to find the override saved on the base group key. The agent silently falls back to the default `gpt-5.4` model configured in `config.yaml`.

---

### Bug 2: Session Split (Context Compression) Discards In-Memory Overrides

When a conversation history reaches the context limit, `AIAgent._compress_context()` triggers a session split in SQLite and rotates `agent.session_id` (e.g. from `192e06e9` to `24b8dc`).

1. **How it fails:**
   The `AIAgent` instance is re-initialized or split, but the session split callback inside the gateway loop does not propagate the active session-only `model_override` to the new session's initialization kwargs.
   
2. **The Mismatch:**
   Since the split session is treated as a new runtime context, it initializes from the global config defaults in `config.yaml`. Any active in-memory `/model` switches are wiped, silently reverting the active model back to the global default mid-conversation, right after a compression turn.

---

### Proposed Fixes

1. **For Bug 1 (Thread Suffix):** 
   In `gateway/run.py` -> `_on_model_selected`, ensure the `session_key` is resolved using the thread ID if the callback originates from a forum chat, so the override key matches the message routing key.

2. **For Bug 2 (Session Split):** 
   Ensure that `_session_model_overrides` is copied/propagated when `_session_was_split` is detected, or preserve the overridden model configurations across context compactions.

3. **User Notification Feature Request:**
   Whenever the model used for the current turn differs from the model used in the previous turn of the same chat, the gateway should append a system notice at the end of the text response (e.g., `[System Notice: Active model changed from X to Y]`) to prevent silent, high-token quota consumption on secondary providers.

The files exist at the expected location — the index just needs `repo` populated (e.g. `NousResearch/hermes-agent`) and `path` updated to `optional-skills/finance/<skill>`.

items.body:
## Bug: `extract_media()` doesn't support `.html`/`.htm` extensions — inconsistent with `extract_local_files()`

## Summary

After the "deliverable mode" PR (#27813, commit `f2fdb9a1`), `MEDIA:/path/to/file.html` no longer delivers the file as a native attachment. The path is left as literal text in the response instead.

## Root Cause

The PR removed a `|\S+` fallback catch-all from the `extract_media()` regex in `gateway/platforms/base.py` to reduce false positives. However, it did **not** add `.html`/`.htm` to the explicit extension list.

Meanwhile, the same PR **did** add `.html`/`.htm` to `extract_local_files()` (the bare-path detector). This means:

| Method | Input example | `.html` supported? |
|---|---|---|
| `extract_media()` | `MEDIA:/home/user/report.html` | ❌ No |
| `extract_local_files()` | `/home/user/report.html` | ✅ Yes |

Both methods ultimately route through the same `send_document()` call, so there's no technical reason to exclude `.html` from `extract_media()`.

Additionally, `gateway/run.py` has two inline `_TOOL_MEDIA_RE` regex patterns (around lines 16562 and 16858) used to scan tool results for MEDIA tags — these also lack `.html`/`.htm`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have Hermes running with Telegram connected.
2. Ask the agent to send an `.html` file using `MEDIA:` tag, e.g.:  
   `MEDIA:/home/user/report.html`
3. Observe: the response text contains the literal `MEDIA:/home/user/report.html` string — no file is delivered.

## Expected Behavior

The `.html` file should be delivered as a native document attachment, consistent with how `extract_local_files()` already handles bare `.html` paths.

## Affected Files

items.body:
## Bug Description
  
`MEDIA:` tags whose file path has an uppercase extension (e.g. .JPG, .PNG, .MP4) are silently dropped. The file is never delivered, and the raw `MEDIA:…` text is stripped from the message body later, so if a response was just the `MEDIA:` tag then the user receives no message. 

## Steps to Reproduce
  
1. Place a real file at e.g. `/Users/me/photo.JPG` (note the uppercase extension)
2. Get the agent to emit `MEDIA:/Users/me/photo.JPG` in a response, eg. ask it directly to send that file by absolute path on any gateway platform.
3. Observe the message the user receives.

Repeat with `/Users/me/photo.jpg` (lowercase) to confirm it otherwise works with a lowercase extension 

## Expected Behavior 
  
The file is uploaded natively to the platform, identically to the .jpg case. The extractor should treat the extension list as case-insensitive. 

## Actual Behavior
No file is delivered. The `MEDIA:/Users/me/photo.JPG` text is also stripped from the response body, so the user sees an empty message (or surrounding prose with no file attachment and no indication anything was supposed to be sent). Nothing is logged at a level that surfaces the silent drop.

## Affected Component

Gateway

## Messaging Platform

All gateway platforms. The bug is in the shared base class (`gateway/platforms/base.py`) not in any platform adapter. 

## Root Cause Analysis

At `gateway/platforms/base.py:2161` the `re.compile(...)` call for `media_pattern` has no flags argument. The extension alternation is:

```
(?:png|jpe?g|gif|webp|mp4|mov|avi|mkv|webm|ogg|opus|mp3|wav|m4a|flac|epub|pdf|zip|rar|7z|docx?|xlsx?|pptx?|txt|csv|apk|ipa)
```

which matches all lowercase. Uppercase paths never match, so `extract_media` returns an empty media list and leaves the response text unchanged.

The miss is then masked by two downstream cleanups that strip `MEDIA:\s*\S+` unconditionally (no extension list, no case constraint):

- `gateway/platforms/base.py:3175` — `text_content = re.sub(r"MEDIA:\s*\S+","", text_content).strip()`
- ``gateway/stream_consumer.py:645`` — ``_MEDIA_RE = re.compile(r'''[`"']?MEDIA:\s*\S+[`"']?''')``

Because these strips succeed where the extractor failed, the user is left with no file and no visible tag meaning no signal that anything was lost.

For reference, the companion `extract_local_files` at `gateway/platforms/base.py:2227` (which detects bare local paths in agent output) is already compiled with `re.IGNORECASE`, so it doesn't exhibit this issue.

## Proposed Fix

Add `re.IGNORECASE` to the `re.compile()` call at `gateway/platforms/base.py:2161`:

```python
media_pattern = re.compile(
    r'''[`"']?MEDIA:\s*(?P<path>`[^`\n]+`|"[^"\n]+"|'[^'\n]+'|(?:~/|/)\S+(?:[^\S\n]+\S+)*?\.(?:png|jpe?g|gif|webp|mp4|mov|avi|mkv|webm|ogg|opus|mp3|wav|m4a|flac|epub|pdf|zip|rar|7z|docx?|xlsx?|pptx?|txt|csv|apk|ipa)(?=[\s`"',;:)\]}]|$))[`"']?''',
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
```
