items.title: background_review fork omits `reasoning_config`, sends different `thinking` field than parent — fragments Anthropic prefix cache (~38% of total cache-write tokens)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
# Background skill/memory review fork sends a different `thinking` field than the parent — fragments Anthropic prefix cache, ~38% of total cache-write tokens

## Summary

The background skill/memory-review fork (`agent/background_review.py`, spawned every `memory_nudge_interval` / `skill_nudge_interval` turns) constructs its child `AIAgent` without propagating `reasoning_config` from the parent. The fork's default `reasoning_config=None` causes `build_anthropic_kwargs` (`agent/anthropic_adapter.py`) to omit the top-level `thinking` and `output_config` fields from the fork's request body, while the parent's request — which has the parent's non-None `reasoning_config` — sends them.

Anthropic's prompt cache is namespaced by the presence of `thinking` in the request body. The divergence forks the cache lineage and forces a full prefix rewrite on every review-fork "birth" call (the first request after spawning), even though the fork shares `messages[0..N]`, `system`, and `tools[]` with the parent byte-for-byte after the fixes in PR #25434 and PR #29704.

This is the same class of bug as #25322 / PR #17276 (`system`-bytes invariant) and #29567 / PR #29704 (`tools[]` invariant), one slot up the cache hierarchy.

## Reproduction

Tested by routing the Anthropic API through a local HTTP-capture proxy (https://github.com/ziliangpeng/midagent — a tiny FastAPI logger that records request_body + response_body) and inspecting the outbound `/v1/messages` requests during a long real-world session that mixes main-agent turns with background review nudges.

Fork-shape requests are easy to identify in any captured traffic: they (a) carry one of the `_SKILL_REVIEW_PROMPT` / `_MEMORY_REVIEW_PROMPT` / `_COMBINED_REVIEW_PROMPT` constants as the last user message, and (b) omit `thinking` / `output_config` at the top level when the parent has reasoning enabled.

In a single ~2-day session window on a Sonnet-class model with `reasoning_config={"enabled": True, "effort": "medium"}` on the parent:

| Slot | Main-turn reqs | Review-fork reqs |
|---|---|---|
| `thinking` top-level key | `{"type":"adaptive","display":"summarized"}` | absent |
| `output_config` top-level key | `{"effort":"medium"}` | absent |
| Last-user-message prefix | normal user text | `"Review the conversation above and update the skill library…"` |
| `cache_read_input_tokens` per "birth" req | n/a (this is the bug surface) | **0** |
| `cache_creation_input_tokens` per "birth" req | small | **dominant** |

## Cost-impact measurement

From the same captured 2-day window (~2,040 `/v1/messages` requests total):

| Quantity | Main reqs | Review-fork reqs (all) | of which fork "birth" |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Request count | 1,389 | 650 | 72 |
| `cache_creation_input_tokens` total | 8.77 M | 11.96 M | **7.82 M** |
| `cache_read_input_tokens` total | 133.07 M | 96.38 M | 0 |

**Of the 20.73 M total `cache_creation_input_tokens` across the window, 7.82 M (≈ 37.7%) came from fork-birth requests alone** — the single request immediately after each `_spawn_background_review`. These are the requests the proposed fix converts from `cache_creation` to `cache_read`, because they share everything with the parent up to the appended `Review the conversation above…` user message but currently land in a different cache namespace.

The 4.14 M `cache_creation_input_tokens` attributable to fork-followup requests (within the spawned review-fork's own iteration loop) is not affected by this fix — those requests already hit the fork's own warmed cache once the birth call lands, and the followup cache-write activity comes from the fork's growing message list per its internal iterations. They are listed for completeness.

The percentage is model-pricing-independent. On Opus pricing the dollar value is substantially higher than on Sonnet for the same token counts, but the structural inefficiency (fork rewrites instead of reading) is identical.

## Root cause

`agent/background_review.py`, inside `_spawn_background_review` (around line 396, after the #29704 fix landed), constructs the review fork as:

```python
review_agent = AIAgent(
    model=agent.model,
    max_iterations=16,
    quiet_mode=True,
    platform=agent.platform,
    provider=agent.provider,
    api_mode=_parent_api_mode,
    base_url=_parent_runtime.get("base_url") or None,
    api_key=_parent_runtime.get("api_key") or None,
    credential_pool=getattr(agent, "_credential_pool", None),
    parent_session_id=agent.session_id,
    enabled_toolsets=getattr(agent, "enabled_toolsets", None),
    disabled_toolsets=getattr(agent, "disabled_toolsets", None),
    skip_memory=True,
)
```

`reasoning_config` is not passed. The `AIAgent.__init__` default is `None`, which makes the request-build path in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py:build_anthropic_kwargs` (around line 2165) skip the entire `thinking` / `output_config` block:

```python
if reasoning_config and isinstance(reasoning_config, dict) and not _is_kimi_coding:
    if reasoning_config.get("enabled") is not False and "haiku" not in model.lower():
        ...
        kwargs["thinking"] = {"type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized"}
        kwargs["output_config"] = {"effort": adaptive_effort}
```

So the parent's narrower / explicit configuration is silently dropped on the fork's outbound request.

PR #17276 (`system` bytes, #25434) and PR #29704 (`tools[]`, #29568) explicitly fixed adjacent slots of this same cache-parity invariant; the `reasoning_config` slot was missed in both rounds.

Direct API verification (independent of Hermes) that `thinking` is part of the cache key:

```
T1: same prompt, thinking=enabled, fresh     cache_read=     0   cache_write= 24026
T2: same prompt, thinking=enabled, repeat    cache_read= 24026   cache_write=     0
T3: same prompt, thinking removed            cache_read=     0   cache_write= 24004    ← bug surface
T4: same prompt, thinking removed, repeat    cache_read= 24004   cache_write=     0
T5: same prompt, thinking=enabled again      cache_read= 24026   cache_write=     0    ← old namespace still warm
```

Both namespaces coexist server-side; the cost is the first flip per direction, which is exactly what every fork-birth pays today.

## Proposed fix

One-line change in `_spawn_background_review`: propagate `reasoning_config` from the parent.

```python
review_agent = AIAgent(
    ...
    enabled_toolsets=getattr(agent, "enabled_toolsets", None),
    disabled_toolsets=getattr(agent, "disabled_toolsets", None),
    skip_memory=True,
    reasoning_config=getattr(agent, "reasoning_config", None),
)
```

Symmetric inheritance — whatever the parent has, the fork gets the same. When the parent's value is `None`, the fork's is also `None` and both omit `thinking` identically; when the parent has reasoning enabled, the fork inherits it verbatim and both land in the same cache namespace.

The post-construction runtime whitelist (`set_thread_tool_whitelist({memory, skills, …})`) installed a few lines below already gates which tools the model can dispatch, so the safety contract from #15204 is unaffected — only what the request body transmits over the wire is being aligned.

## Verification

After applying the fix (same conversation, same model, reasoning enabled on the parent):

| Window | Total fork-birth reqs | Distinct `thinking`-presence values across main + fork |
|---|---:|---:|
| Pre-fix | 72 | **2** (parent has `thinking`, fork omits it) |
| Post-fix | new fork-birth reqs | **1** (identical) |

Captured fork-birth requests post-fix carry `thinking: {"type":"adaptive","display":"summarized"}` and `output_config: {"effort":"medium"}` identical to the parent's, and their `cache_read_input_tokens` jumps from 0 to ≈ the full shared prefix.

The accompanying PR adds a positive assertion `test_review_fork_inherits_parent_reasoning_config` to `tests/run_agent/test_background_review_cache_parity.py` (the same file that covers PR #17276 and PR #29704's invariants) so future regressions of the same shape are caught at test time.

## Scope of the fix

- `agent/background_review.py`: one added kwarg + one-line comment.
- `tests/run_agent/test_background_review_cache_parity.py`: new positive assertion, stub updated to carry a non-`None` `reasoning_config` so a missing-kwarg regression surfaces.
- No production code paths outside the review fork; no schema or public-API changes; safety whitelist untouched.

items.body:
## Bug

`_recover_telegram_topic_thread_id()` redirects messages from a DM topic that has an active session but no binding into the user's most-recent topic binding.

When a user has multiple DM topic sessions active simultaneously (e.g. General/System lobby + a named lane like "English"), messages sent to the lobby topic get routed to the named lane session instead.

### Root cause

The recovery function checks two conditions before redirecting:
1. Is the inbound thread_id in `_TELEGRAM_GENERAL_TOPIC_IDS` (hardcoded to `{"", "1"}`)?
2. Is the inbound thread_id in the `bindings` table?

For DM topics, the General/System lobby thread_id is dynamically assigned by Telegram (e.g. `494403`) and is NOT in `_TELEGRAM_GENERAL_TOPIC_IDS`. It also doesn't appear in `telegram_dm_topic_bindings` because bindings only track named lane topics created via `/topic`.

So the lobby passes both checks → recovery finds the newest binding → redirects to that session.

### Reproduction

1. Enable DM topic mode (`/topic`)
2. Create a named topic lane (e.g. "English")
3. Send a message in the General/System lobby topic
4. Send a message in the named lane
5. Send another message in the lobby → observe it gets routed to the named lane session

Log evidence:
```
telegram topic recovery: chat=123456789 user=123456789 '494403' -> 494621
```

### Fix

Before redirecting, also check if the inbound thread_id has an existing session (either a running agent or a persisted session in the session store). If it does, don't redirect — the user intentionally wrote to that topic.

```python
# Check running agents first (fast path)
if session_key in self._running_agents:
    return None
# Check session store for an existing session
self.session_store._ensure_loaded()
if session_key in self.session_store._entries:
    return None
```

### Impact

Breaks multi-topic parallel session isolation in Telegram DMs. Users experience cross-topic replies where messages sent to one topic get answered in the context of another, causing confusion and breaking topic-specific configurations (skills, models, etc.).

items.title: discord/discord_admin tools silently hidden when DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN is only in .env
items.body:
**Summary:** The `discord` and `discord_admin` toolsets are gated by
`requires_env=["DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN"]` and
`check_fn=check_discord_tool_requirements()`, which calls
`os.getenv("DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN")`. However, `~/.hermes/.env` is not
loaded into `os.environ` before tool availability is evaluated during
gateway startup. This causes both toolsets to be silently filtered
out — no warning in logs, no entry in `hermes tools` config menu,
and the agent never sees `fetch_messages`, `list_channels`, or any
of the 15 discord tool actions.

**Reproduction:**
1. Fresh install, configure Discord gateway via `hermes gateway setup`
2. Confirm `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` is in `~/.hermes/.env`
3. Start gateway: `hermes gateway`
4. Ask the agent to list its tools — `discord` and `discord_admin`
   are absent
5. Stop gateway, run `export DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=$(grep
   DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN ~/.hermes/.env | cut -d= -f2)`, restart gateway
6. Ask again — both toolsets now appear and work correctly

**Root cause:** `env_loader.py` / `load_dotenv()` runs after
`discover_builtin_tools()` (called at import time from
`model_tools.py:180`) or after `check_tool_availability()` evaluates
`requires_env`. The token IS in `.env` but not yet in `os.environ`
when the check runs.

**Workaround:** Export `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` in shell profile
(`.zshrc`/`.bashrc`) before starting the gateway.

**Suggested fix:** Either:
(a) Move `load_dotenv(~/.hermes/.env)` earlier in the startup
    sequence — before any tool discovery or availability checks, OR
(b) Have `check_tool_availability()` and `get_definitions()` call
    `_get_bot_token()` with a fallback that reads `~/.hermes/.env`
    directly if the env var is missing, OR
(c) Log a warning when a toolset is filtered out due to missing
    `requires_env` vars, so users can diagnose the issue.

**Environment:** Hermes Agent v0.14.0 (2026.5.16), macOS, Python
3.11.14, discord.py 2.7.1

**Impact:** Affects any user relying on the default `.env`-based
Discord token configuration. The `discord` toolset contains
`fetch_messages` — a key capability for cross-channel reading —
which is completely invisible until the user manually exports the
token.

items.title: macOS: launchd domain hardcodes gui/ — breaks gateway and setup for SSH-only / non-console users

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, `_launchd_domain()` in `hermes_cli/gateway.py` hardcodes `gui/{uid}` as the launchd domain. This domain does not exist for users who don't own the console session (i.e. SSH-only accounts, shared Mac minis, headless CI runners). The issue manifests in **both `gateway` and `setup`** commands.

## Environment

- macOS (reproduced on macOS 26.x, Ventura and later)
- User connected via SSH only (non-console UID)
- Another user owns the loginwindow / Aqua session
- `launchctl print gui/<uid>` returns: `125: Domain does not support specified action`

## Affected commands

### 1. `hermes gateway restart` / `hermes gateway start`

```
$ hermes gateway restart
Could not kickstart service "ai.hermes.gateway": 125: Domain does not support specified action
✗ Gateway service restart failed.
```

Every `launchctl kickstart`, `bootout`, and `bootstrap` call goes through `_launchd_domain()` which returns `gui/<uid>`. The service may already be loaded in `user/<uid>` (e.g. from a previous `gateway install` that happened to succeed), but the CLI cannot control it.

### 2. `hermes setup` (gateway section)

The setup wizard calls `gateway install`, which also uses `_launchd_domain()`. On affected machines the bootstrap into `gui/{uid}` either fails silently or produces the "Domain does not support specified action" error, leaving the user with no working gateway and no clear next step.

## Root cause

```python
# hermes_cli/gateway.py:2779
def _launchd_domain() -> str:
    return f"gui/{os.getuid()}"
```

`gui/{uid}` is only available when the user has an active Aqua (GUI login) session. For SSH-only, `screen`/`tmux`, or headless accounts, this domain is absent. The correct fallback is `user/{uid}`, which is always available.

## Suggested fix

Probe `gui/{uid}` first and fall back to `user/{uid}`:

```python
def _launchd_domain() -> str:
    uid = os.getuid()
    gui_domain = f"gui/{uid}"
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["launchctl", "print", gui_domain],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
        )
        if result.returncode == 0:
            return gui_domain
    except Exception:
        pass
    return f"user/{uid}"
```

Additionally, the generated plist should include `LimitLoadToSessionType` so the service is allowed to start in non-Aqua sessions:

```xml
<key>LimitLoadToSessionType</key>
<array>
    <string>Aqua</string>
    <string>StandardIO</string>
    <string>Background</string>
</array>
```

Without this, launchd may refuse to start the job in SSH/headless sessions even if the domain is correct.

## Workaround

Manually patch `_launchd_domain()` and regenerate the plist with `hermes gateway install`. A future `hermes update` will overwrite the patch.

## Impact

Anyone running Hermes on a shared macOS machine where they are not the console user — fairly common for Mac mini servers, CI runners, and homelab setups.

items.title: feat: Adaptive retry with model escalation and owner notification for kanban dispatcher

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Summary

The kanban dispatcher currently retries failed tasks identically — same profile, same model, same prompt. When a task hits a non-trivial failure (not a deterministic config error like #30417, but a genuinely hard problem), retrying with the exact same setup is wasteful. The dispatcher should progressively adapt its retry strategy.

Related: #30417 covers the circuit breaker not tripping on deterministic spawn failures. This issue is complementary — it addresses what happens on the _retry path_ before the breaker trips, and what happens _after_ it trips.

## Problem

Three gaps in the current retry/failure lifecycle:

### 1. Retries are identical (no learning from failure)

When a worker crashes or times out, `_record_task_failure` increments `consecutive_failures` and the dispatcher respawns with the identical prompt, model, and context. The worker has no knowledge of why the previous attempt failed, so it hits the same wall.

**Desired:** On retry, inject the previous attempt's error/summary into the worker's context:
```
## Previous Attempt Failed
Your previous attempt failed with: [error excerpt]
Previous output: [truncated summary from last run]
Try a different approach.
```

This is cheap (just prepend to the worker's system context from `runs.error` / `runs.summary`) and dramatically increases the chance of a different outcome.

### 2. No model escalation on consecutive failures

If a task fails twice with a cheaper model (e.g., `sonnet`), the third attempt should try a stronger model (e.g., `opus`) before giving up. The `model_override` field already exists on tasks — the dispatcher just needs to set it on retry.

**Desired:** A configurable escalation ladder:
```yaml
kanban:
  retry_model_escalation:
    sonnet4.6-off: sonnet4.6-low    # attempt 2: add thinking
    sonnet4.6-low: opus4.6-high      # attempt 3: upgrade model
```

The dispatcher reads this on each retry and sets `model_override` accordingly. If no escalation is configured, behavior is unchanged (same model, backwards compatible).

### 3. No notification on `gave_up` or stale `blocked`

When a task exhausts retries and transitions to `gave_up` (or sits in `blocked` for hours), nobody is notified. The task silently rots on the board until a human checks.

**Desired:** The existing kanban notifier (`kanban_notify_subs` in the gateway) should emit notifications for `gave_up` events, not just `completed` and `blocked`. The notification target is already configurable via `kanban.notify_target`.

For `blocked` tasks that have been stuck beyond a configurable threshold (e.g., 2 hours), the notifier should also emit a stale-alert.

## Proposed Implementation

### Tier 1 — Retry with failure context (low effort)
In the dispatcher's spawn path, when `consecutive_failures > 0`, read the most recent `runs.error` and `runs.summary` for the task and inject them into the worker's prompt context (e.g., via `--prefill` or an env var the kanban-worker skill reads).

### Tier 2 — Model escalation (medium effort)
Add `kanban.retry_model_escalation` config (dict mapping model → upgrade). On retry, if the current model has an escalation target, set `model_override` on the task before spawning.

### Tier 3 — Notification on gave_up / stale blocked (medium effort)
Extend `_emit_kanban_notifications` (or equivalent) to include `gave_up` events. Add a configurable `kanban.stale_blocked_alert_seconds` threshold for periodic stale-block alerts.

## Context

We run a multi-profile kanban setup (v0.14.0, macOS) with ~20 tasks/day across several profiles. Tasks that require cross-domain knowledge or encounter unexpected environments frequently fail twice and give up silently. The workaround is a cron-based board watchdog, but native dispatcher support would benefit all users running multi-agent kanban workflows.

items.body:
## Bug

`hermes update` refreshes active lazy backends via `tools/lazy_deps._venv_pip_install`, which fails with PEP 668 `externally-managed-environment` when Hermes is installed against a system Python (no venv) on PEP 668 distros (Debian/Ubuntu/Kali base images).

The previous PEP 668 fix in #2648 covered the main `hermes update` install path but not the lazy-deps refresh introduced when `[all]` was slimmed down in May 2026.

## Repro

Container based on Kali rolling (`python3 --version` = 3.13.12, system pip with PEP 668 marker). Hermes installed via `pip install --user`, no venv.

```
$ hermes update
...
→ Refreshing 16 active lazy backend(s)...
  ⚠ platform.discord failed to refresh: pip install failed: error: externally-managed-environment
  ⚠ platform.telegram failed to refresh: pip install failed: error: externally-managed-environment
  ⚠ platform.dingtalk failed to refresh: pip install failed: error: externally-managed-environment
  ⚠ platform.feishu failed to refresh: pip install failed: error: externally-managed-environment
  ⚠ tool.dashboard failed to refresh: pip install failed: error: externally-managed-environment
  Backends keep their previously-installed version; rerun
  `hermes update` once the upstream issue is resolved.
```

The platforms stay on their previously-installed versions and keep working, but they never pick up upstream pin bumps (including CVE backports).

## Root cause

`tools/lazy_deps.py:_venv_pip_install`:

- **Tier 1 (uv):** sets `VIRTUAL_ENV = Path(sys.executable).parent.parent`. When `sys.executable` is `/usr/bin/python3` that resolves to `/usr`, which uv (correctly) rejects/falls through.
- **Tier 2 (`python -m pip install …`):** invokes the system pip directly. PEP 668 distros refuse.

Neither tier passes `--break-system-packages`, `--user`, or detects "we're not actually in a venv" before trying.

```
$ python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.executable, sys.prefix == sys.base_prefix)"
/usr/bin/python3 True
```

## Suggested fix

In `_venv_pip_install`, detect non-venv interpreter (`sys.prefix == sys.base_prefix`) and:

1. Re-use the same install ladder `hermes_cli/main.py` uses for the main update path (which was fixed in #2648), OR
2. Fall back to `pip install --user` when running against system Python, OR
3. Pass `--break-system-packages` as last resort with a clear warning.

Option 1 is cleanest — `_install_python_dependencies_with_optional_fallback` already knows how to handle this for the base install; lazy_deps should call into the same helper rather than reimplementing the ladder.

## Environment

- OS: Kali rolling 2026.1 (Docker, PEP 668)
- Python: 3.13.12 (system, no venv)
- Hermes: v0.14.0 → updated to latest main
- Install method: `pip install --user hermes-agent`
- uv: present (`/config/.local/bin/uv`)

## Workaround

Backends still function on prior pins. Manual refresh: `pip install --break-system-packages --upgrade <pkg>` per affected feature.

## Related

- #2648 (closed, same root cause but for main update path)

items.title: MCP tool results with EmbeddedResource (resource) blocks are silently dropped
items.body:
## Summary

MCP tool results that contain `resource` blocks (`EmbeddedResource`) are silently dropped. For an `EmbeddedResource`, the payload text lives on `block.resource.text`, **not** `block.text`. The result handler in `tools/mcp_tool.py` only checks `block.text` and `_cache_mcp_image_block`, so any MCP server whose tool returns a resource block yields an empty `{"result": ""}` and the agent gets nothing.

## Reproduction

Any MCP server that returns an `EmbeddedResource` content block triggers this. Concrete example: the [`qmd`](https://github.com/) MCP server's `get` tool returns its document as a single resource block:

```json
"content": [{
  "type": "resource",
  "resource": {
    "uri": "qmd://obsidian/note.md",
    "mimeType": "text/markdown",
    "text": "<full document text>"
  }
}]
```

Calling that tool through Hermes returns `{"result": ""}`. The server is behaving correctly per the MCP spec — `EmbeddedResource` is a valid content block type. Sibling tools on the same server that return plain `text` blocks (e.g. `query`, `status`) work fine, which confirms the issue is block-type-specific.

## Root cause

`_make_tool_handler` in `tools/mcp_tool.py` handles `text` blocks and image blocks, but not `resource` blocks. The outer block has no `.text` attribute, so it falls through to `_cache_mcp_image_block`, which returns `None`, and the content is discarded. Both the success path (~line 2274) and the error path (~line 2243) have the bug.

## Fix

Add an `EmbeddedResource` branch on both paths that unwraps `block.resource.text`. `TextResourceContents` exposes `.text`; `BlobResourceContents` exposes `.blob` (not handled here — out of scope, but noted).

```diff
diff --git a/tools/mcp_tool.py b/tools/mcp_tool.py
@@ -2243,8 +2243,15 @@ def _make_tool_handler(server_name, tool_name, tool_timeout):
             if result.isError:
                 error_text = ""
                 for block in (result.content or []):
-                    if hasattr(block, "text"):
+                    if hasattr(block, "text") and block.text:
                         error_text += block.text
+                        continue
+                    # EmbeddedResource blocks carry text one level down.
+                    embedded = getattr(block, "resource", None)
+                    if embedded is not None:
+                        res_text = getattr(embedded, "text", None)
+                        if res_text:
+                            error_text += res_text
                 return json.dumps({
                     "error": _sanitize_error(
                         error_text or "MCP tool returned an error"
@@ -2267,6 +2274,18 @@ def _make_tool_handler(server_name, tool_name, tool_timeout):
                 if hasattr(block, "text") and block.text:
                     parts.append(block.text)
                     continue
+                # EmbeddedResource blocks (MCP `type: "resource"`) carry their
+                # payload one level down on `.resource`: TextResourceContents
+                # exposes `.text`, BlobResourceContents exposes `.blob`.
+                # Without this branch, servers that return resource blocks
+                # (e.g. qmd's `get` tool) yield an empty result because the
+                # outer block has no `.text` attribute.
+                embedded = getattr(block, "resource", None)
+                if embedded is not None:
+                    res_text = getattr(embedded, "text", None)
+                    if res_text:
+                        parts.append(res_text)
+                        continue
                 image_tag = _cache_mcp_image_block(block)
                 if image_tag:
                     parts.append(image_tag)
```

Verified against real MCP SDK types (`EmbeddedResource` + `TextResourceContents`): the fix extracts the text, and plain `text` blocks still work unchanged. Two regression tests added to `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py` (`test_embedded_resource_result`, `test_embedded_resource_error_result`); the full `test_mcp_tool.py` suite passes (195 tests).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `main` (commit `05af78c53`)
- macOS, Python 3.11

items.body:
## Bug Description

Several model-picker unit tests are not hermetic when a local Ollama-compatible server is reachable on `http://localhost:11434/v1`. The tests pass explicit `custom_providers` with small expected model lists, but `list_authenticated_providers()` probes live custom endpoints whenever an API key is present. In the common local-Ollama case (`api_key: "ollama"`), the probe replaces the configured test models with the real local `/models` catalog, causing deterministic assertion failures on developer/cron machines that have Ollama running.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run an Ollama-compatible OpenAI endpoint on `localhost:11434` with any models loaded.
2. Check out latest `main` (`09afafb87e486eea62de0d7892a127808f121b0a` during this hunt).
3. Run either:
   ```bash
   venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_model_switch_custom_providers.py::test_list_authenticated_providers_groups_same_endpoint -q
   ```
   or the full suite:
   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh -j 12
   ```

## Expected Behavior

The unit tests should be independent of locally running model servers. They should either mock `fetch_api_models()` or otherwise force the function under test to preserve the explicitly supplied `custom_providers` list.

## Actual Behavior

With local Ollama running, the targeted test fails because the row's models come from the live server instead of the fixture:

```text
E       AssertionError: assert {'gemma4:e4b-...:4b-gpu', ...} == {'glm-5.1', '...'qwen3-coder'}
E         Extra items in the left set:
E         'hf.co/Jackrong/Qwopus3.5-9B-v3-GGUF:Q4_K_M'
E         'gemma4:e4b-gpu'
E         'nomic-embed-text:latest'
E         'qwopus3.5:9b-gpu'
E         'qwen3.5:4b'...
```

The same root cause caused these failures in the full cron run:

```text
tests/hermes_cli/test_list_picker_providers.py::test_current_custom_endpoint_passthrough_marks_current_row
tests/hermes_cli/test_model_switch_custom_providers.py::test_list_authenticated_providers_groups_same_endpoint
tests/hermes_cli/test_model_switch_custom_providers.py::test_list_authenticated_providers_distinct_endpoints_stay_separate
tests/hermes_cli/test_model_switch_custom_providers.py::test_list_authenticated_provider_duplicate_name_distinct_url_gets_suffix
```

## Root Cause Evidence

`hermes_cli/model_switch.py` section 4 computes:

```python
should_probe = bool(api_url) and (bool(api_key) or not grp["models"])
```

The test fixtures use `api_key: "ollama"`, so `should_probe` is true even though the fixtures also provide explicit `model` values. When `fetch_api_models(api_key, api_url)` succeeds against a developer's live Ollama endpoint, it overwrites `grp["models"]`.

## Environment

- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Branch/ref: `main` at `09afafb87e486eea62de0d7892a127808f121b0a`
- Host: WSL/Linux with local Ollama-compatible endpoint on `localhost:11434`
- Test runner: `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 12` and targeted `venv/bin/python -m pytest ...`

## Suggested Fix

Mock `hermes_cli.models.fetch_api_models` in these tests (or add a test-only parameter/env guard) so unit expectations cannot be changed by live localhost services. If live discovery is intentional runtime behavior, keep that covered by separate tests with explicit mocked responses.

items.title: ui-tui type-check fails in execFileNoThrow stdioConfig overload resolution
items.body:
## Bug Description

`ui-tui`'s declared TypeScript type-check script fails on current `main` even though the bundle build still succeeds. The failure is isolated to `packages/hermes-ink/src/utils/execFileNoThrow.ts`: `stdioConfig` is inferred as a union containing a readonly tuple (`['pipe', 'ignore', 'ignore'] as const`) and `'pipe'`, which does not match Node's mutable `StdioOptions`. After that overload mismatch, TypeScript narrows the spawned child to `never`, producing cascading errors for `stdout`, `stderr`, `kill`, `on`, and `stdin`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out latest `main` (`09afafb87e486eea62de0d7892a127808f121b0a` during this hunt).
2. Run:
   ```bash
   cd ui-tui
   npm run type-check
   ```

## Expected Behavior

`npm run type-check` exits 0 for the checked-in TypeScript sources.

## Actual Behavior

The command exits 2. First errors:

```text
packages/hermes-ink/src/utils/execFileNoThrow.ts(42,7): error TS2769: No overload matches this call.
  The last overload gave the following error.
    Type '"pipe" | readonly ["pipe", "ignore", "ignore"]' is not assignable to type 'StdioOptions | undefined'.
      Type 'readonly ["pipe", "ignore", "ignore"]' is not assignable to type 'StdioOptions | undefined'.
        The type 'readonly ["pipe", "ignore", "ignore"]' is 'readonly' and cannot be assigned to the mutable type '(number | Stream | IOType | "ipc" | null | undefined)[]'.
packages/hermes-ink/src/utils/execFileNoThrow.ts(63,13): error TS2339: Property 'stdout' does not exist on type 'never'.
packages/hermes-ink/src/utils/execFileNoThrow.ts(64,13): error TS2339: Property 'stderr' does not exist on type 'never'.
packages/hermes-ink/src/utils/execFileNoThrow.ts(72,17): error TS2339: Property 'kill' does not exist on type 'never'.
...
```

`npm run build` in the same directory still exits 0, so this is a type-check regression rather than an immediate bundling failure.

## Environment

- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Branch/ref: `main` at `09afafb87e486eea62de0d7892a127808f121b0a`
- Host: WSL/Linux
- Command: `npm run type-check` from `ui-tui/`

## Notes / Likely Fix

Give `stdioConfig` an explicit mutable `StdioOptions`/`SpawnOptions['stdio']` type, or avoid `as const` on the tuple branch so Node's `spawn` overload can resolve to a child type with nullable stdio streams instead of `never`.

items.title: [Bug]: WebUI chat send silently fails — _inflightStateLimits name collision between boot.js and ui.js

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

Sending a chat message in the WebUI silently fails — the message appears optimistically in the UI but no `POST /api/chat/start` ever reaches the server. No visible error is shown to the user.

## Root Cause

**Name collision** between `boot.js` and `ui.js`:

1. `ui.js` (loaded first via `defer`) declares `function _inflightStateLimits(){}` at line 4084 — this becomes `window._inflightStateLimits`
2. `boot.js` (loaded last via `defer`) sets `window._inflightStateLimits = {...object...}` at line 1462 — this **overwrites the function** with a config object
3. When `send()` runs → `saveInflightState()` → `_compactInflightState()` → `_inflightStateLimits()` — it's now calling an object, not a function

```
TypeError: _inflightStateLimits is not a function
    at _compactInflightState (ui.js:4128)
    at saveInflightState (ui.js:4159)
    at send (messages.js:421)
```

This crashes `send()` at line 421, **before** the `POST /api/chat/start` at line 450 is ever reached.

## Script Load Order (index.html)

```html
<script src="static/ui.js?v=__WEBUI_VERSION__" defer></script>      <!-- line 1369 -->
<script src="static/messages.js?v=__WEBUI_VERSION__" defer></script> <!-- line 1374 -->
<script src="static/boot.js?v=__WEBUI_VERSION__" defer></script>     <!-- line 1377 -->
```

## Fix

Rename the config property in `boot.js` to `window._inflightStateLimitsConfig` and update `ui.js` to read from `window._inflightStateLimitsConfig` instead of `window._inflightStateLimits`.

**boot.js:1462:**
```diff
-    window._inflightStateLimits={
+    window._inflightStateLimitsConfig={
```

**ui.js:4085:**
```diff
-  const configured=(typeof window!=='undefined'&&window._inflightStateLimits&&typeof window._inflightStateLimits==='object')?window._inflightStateLimits:{};
+  const configured=(typeof window!=='undefined'&&window._inflightStateLimitsConfig&&typeof window._inflightStateLimitsConfig==='object')?window._inflightStateLimitsConfig:{};
```

## Version

v0.51.117

items.title: [Bug]: `hermes -z` oneshot exits 0 silently before API call when stdout is non-TTY pipe (SSH/cron/subprocess)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description

When `hermes -z PROMPT` (oneshot mode) is invoked with `stdout` connected to a non-TTY pipe — for example, the standard case of an SSH `ForceCommand` or any scripted/cron context — the process exits 0 silently. No model API call is made, no response appears on stdout, and the conversation log captures only the user prompt with no assistant reply.

This blocks any use of Hermes as a non-interactive worker (cron, SSH bridge, subprocess invocation from another agent).

### Steps to Reproduce

On Ubuntu 24.04 with `hermes-agent==0.14.0`, after configuring an `openai-codex` OAuth provider:

```bash
source ~/.venv-hermes/bin/activate
hermes -z 'Reply with exactly OK and nothing else.' 2>&1 | head
```

Or equivalently over SSH (forced-command scenario):

```bash
ssh user@host "source ~/.venv-hermes/bin/activate && hermes -z 'test prompt'"
```

### Expected Behavior

- Oneshot mode performs the model call.
- Final assistant response is written to stdout.
- Exit nonzero on fatal setup or runtime error (loud failure, not silent).

### Actual Behavior

- stdout is empty.
- Exit code 0.
- No API call is made (verified — see logs below).
- Session JSON at `~/.hermes/sessions/session_<id>.json` contains only the user message; no assistant response is persisted.
- `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log` shows **no `run_agent: conversation turn` entry** for the oneshot session, confirming the process exits before the agent loop is reached.

### Error Excerpt (from ~/.hermes/logs/errors.log)

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../prompt_toolkit/application/application.py", line 886, in run_async
    return await _run_async(f)
  File ".../prompt_toolkit/application/application.py", line 756, in _run_async
    self.renderer.reset()
  File ".../prompt_toolkit/renderer.py", line 429, in reset
    self.output.flush()
  File ".../prompt_toolkit/output/vt100.py", line 706, in flush
    flush_stdout(self.stdout, data)
  File ".../prompt_toolkit/output/flush_stdout.py", line 37, in flush_stdout
    stdout.flush()
OSError: [Errno 5] Input/output error
```

The exception is raised by `prompt_toolkit`'s `Vt100_Output.flush()` when `stdout.flush()` cannot write to a non-TTY destination. Because oneshot mode unconditionally instantiates the TUI renderer before doing anything else, this crashes the process before the model is even contacted.

### Root Cause Analysis

`hermes -z` should be a non-interactive code path. It should NOT initialize `prompt_toolkit` at all — the TUI renderer is a `hermes chat`/`--tui` concern. The fact that prompt_toolkit's vt100 output is being initialized for oneshot is the actual bug; the Errno 5 is just the visible symptom.

### Workarounds Tested (none worked)

- `HERMES_NONINTERACTIVE=1` (env var found in source at `hermes_cli/web_server.py` and similar — does not gate the prompt_toolkit import on the oneshot path)
- `HERMES_QUIET=1`
- Both combined
- Confirmed: no `--output`, `--headless`, `--no-tui`, `--batch` flag exists on `hermes -z`

### Impact

This blocks any programmatic/scripted use of `hermes -z`:

- SSH `ForceCommand`-style worker bridges (the scenario we hit)
- Cron jobs that need to capture model output
- Subprocess invocation from another agent or orchestrator
- Any non-interactive automation

Interactive use (`hermes` / `hermes chat` / `--tui`) works perfectly — the bug is exclusive to oneshot-over-pipe.

### Suggested Fix

1. Oneshot mode should not initialize the prompt_toolkit renderer at all. Branch the codepath so `-z` skips TUI setup entirely.
2. If TUI setup is unavoidable, detect non-TTY stdout (`not sys.stdout.isatty()`) and use a plain-text fallback writer.
3. Exit nonzero (and surface an error message on stderr) if the oneshot pipeline fails to make an API call. Silent exit-0 on bug is the worst-case failure mode for any automated caller.
4. Add a CI regression test: `hermes -z 'test' | cat` must produce nonempty stdout (or fail loudly).

### Related

This is **distinct from #10755** (WSL2 PTY *disconnect*, where a PTY was present then dropped). Here there is no PTY from the start — the stdout is a pipe by design. Both surface the same `OSError` from `prompt_toolkit`'s flush path but the trigger conditions differ.

### Environment

- Package: hermes-agent 0.14.0 (latest on PyPI as of 2026-05-22)
- Python: 3.12.3
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- prompt_toolkit: 3.0.52 (from hermes-agent install)
- OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
- Provider configured: `openai-codex` (OAuth, working — confirmed by ~50 successful interactive `hermes chat` API calls in the same session)

items.title: state.db corruption from SIGTERM during launchd shutdown under high load

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Agent v0.14.0 on macOS 15.3 (Darwin 25.3.0), single-user single-machine. `state.db` corrupted three times over a 48h window. Reproducible cause identified from logs.

## Trigger

From `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log`, immediately preceding the first corruption:

```
2026-05-20 01:13:31  WARNING gateway.run: Shutdown context:
                     signal=SIGTERM under_systemd=yes parent_pid=1
                     parent_name=? loadavg_1m=13.69 parent_cmdline='(unknown)'
2026-05-20 01:14:04  WARNING [20260520_010451_ca0b1a] run_agent:
                     Session DB append_message failed: database disk image is malformed
```

launchd sent SIGTERM to the gateway while `loadavg_1m=13.69` (system saturated). 33 s later, WAL pages had not been checkpointed and `state.db` went malformed. From that point on, every gateway start logged `SQLite session store not available: database disk image is malformed` and silently fell back to JSONL sidecar sessions — masking the corruption from the user. Telegram-sourced sessions were invisible from `hermes sessions list` because the JSONL fallback only contains CLI sessions.

## Root cause hypothesis

1. **No `PRAGMA synchronous=FULL`**. `hermes_state.py:152` (`apply_wal_with_fallback`) sets `journal_mode=WAL` but never raises synchronous. Default `NORMAL` in WAL mode is vulnerable to OS-level process kills mid-write.
2. **No pre-exit checkpoint in gateway shutdown**. `gateway/run.py` closes `SessionDB` on shutdown (line ~5819) but doesn't force `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`. Combined with `HERMES_SIGTERM_GRACE=1.5s`, there's no guarantee the WAL is flushed before launchd escalates to SIGKILL.
3. **FTS5 trigram index amplifies write pressure and is fragile**. Reproduced manually during DB recovery: `INSERT INTO messages SELECT ...` with FTS triggers active returned `database disk image is malformed (11)` despite both source and target passing `PRAGMA integrity_check`. Dropping the FTS triggers, inserting, then rebuilding `messages_fts_trigram` from scratch succeeded. Suggests the trigram index has stability issues under bulk writes.

## Cascading data loss

Between May 20 and May 22, two automatic recovery attempts shrank `state.db` from 167 MB → 26 MB silently:

| Date | File | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| May 21 13:55 | `state.db.corrupt.20260521_135543.bak` | 167 MB | First corruption snapshot |
| May 21 13:55 | `state.db.recovered.20260521_135543` | 178 MB | First `.recover` output, schema OK |
| May 22 11:45 | `state.db.bak.20260522_114556` | 167 MB | Backup before re-corruption |
| May 22 11:46 | `state.db.repaired` | 37 MB | **Failed `.recover`: only `lost_and_found` table** |
| May 22 17:00 | `state.db.corrupt_latest` | 15 MB | **DB shrank — massive data loss** |
| May 23 00:05 | `state.db` (active) | 26 MB | Only 1080 messages remained out of 14k+ |

Manual recovery: 14,104 messages / 241 sessions reconstructed by `.recover` + chunked re-insert with FTS triggers temporarily disabled, then trigram index rebuilt from scratch. Telegram sessions that had been invisible to `hermes sessions list` are back.

## Suggested fixes

- In `apply_wal_with_fallback`, also `PRAGMA synchronous=FULL` (or at minimum `=EXTRA` for WAL mode)

- Investigate FTS5 trigram index robustness under bulk inserts — at minimum document the workaround (disable triggers → insert → rebuild trigram FTS)

items.title: Slack gateway should treat explicit no-reply sentinels as intentional silence

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

Slack group channels and threads are a shared human surface. A gateway-backed agent may receive events for conversations where the bot is present but is not being directly asked to respond. In those cases, the agent harness may intentionally return an explicit no-reply sentinel such as `NO_REPLY` to mean "leave the thread untouched".

Today, if that sentinel reaches the Slack final-send path, the adapter can treat it like ordinary assistant text and post the literal `NO_REPLY` into Slack. That turns an intentional silent turn into visible channel clutter. It also makes it harder for Slack deployments to use direct-ask gating without requiring a hard mention for every legitimate follow-up.

## Expected behavior

When the final assistant response text is exactly `NO_REPLY` after trimming surrounding whitespace, the Slack gateway should treat the turn as intentional silence:

- do not call Slack `chat.postMessage`
- do not post the literal sentinel into the channel/thread
- do not treat the turn as a generation failure or retryable empty response
- optionally emit a debug log indicating an intentionally suppressed no-reply turn

## Non-goals

- This is not specific to any company, workspace, bot persona, or deployment.
- This does not require Slack bots to only respond to hard mentions.
- This is not a general solution for all empty model outputs.
- This should not suppress ordinary messages that merely contain `NO_REPLY` as part of longer text.

## Proposed implementation

Add a guard in the Slack adapter as close as practical to the final `chat_postMessage` call:

```python
if text.strip() == "NO_REPLY":
    # intentional no-op for Slack
    return
```

The check should be exact after whitespace trimming. Longer messages such as `"I would not use NO_REPLY here"` should still send normally.

## Acceptance criteria

- Slack adapter suppresses exact `NO_REPLY` responses.
- Surrounding whitespace is ignored for the sentinel check.
- Longer messages containing `NO_REPLY` are still posted.
- Suppressed sentinel turns do not call Slack `chat.postMessage`.
- Add a regression test around the Slack send/dispatch path.

## Related context

- #13248 is adjacent: it discusses Slack group-thread behavior around non-replies / empty responses.
- #18073 and #3293 are related background on gateway-delivered agent side-channel notifications, but this issue is specifically about the final Slack response send path and explicit no-reply sentinels.

items.title: Feature Request: Dynamic model routing based on task complexity

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes Agent currently locks each session to a single model via `config.yaml`. This means every request — whether it's "what's the weather" or "design a microservices architecture" — goes through the same model at the same cost/latency.

There's no built-in way to route tasks to different models based on complexity, cost, or capability requirements.

## Current Workaround

Users have to build their own routing layer using:
1. **prefill_messages_file** — inject routing instructions into every session
2. **delegate_task** — spawn subagents with different model overrides for complex tasks
3. **Manual skill management** — maintain routing rules externally

This works but is fragile, requires significant setup, and duplicates logic that should be in core.

## Proposed Solution

Add native dynamic model routing to Hermes Agent, for example:

### Option A: Routing rules in config.yaml
```yaml
model_routing:
  default: local/qwen3-6b  # cheap/free baseline
  
  rules:
    - match: "complexity > 7"
      provider: openrouter
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
    
    - match: "needs_vision"
      provider: openrouter  
      model: qwen/qwen3-vl-plus
    
    - match: "token_estimate > 5000"
      provider: openai-codex
      model: gpt-5.5
```

### Option B: Agent-accessible model switching
Allow agents to call a tool like `model_switch(provider, model)` mid-session when they detect a task exceeds the current model's capabilities.

### Option C: Delegation auto-routing
When `delegate_task` is called without explicit model override, automatically select an appropriate model based on task description complexity.

## Benefits

- **Cost savings**: Route simple queries to cheap/local models, complex work to frontier models
- **Better performance**: Use specialized models for specific tasks (vision, coding, reasoning)
- **Improved UX**: Users don't need to manually select models or maintain external routing skills
- **Competitive advantage**: Other agent frameworks don't have this — it would be a differentiator

## Current State

This feature gap means users either:
1. Always use expensive frontier models (wasteful for simple tasks)
2. Always use cheap models (fails on complex tasks)
3. Build fragile workarounds with prefill + delegation

## Related

- The `prefill_messages_file` config option exists but isn't documented as a routing mechanism
- `delegate_task` supports model overrides but requires manual decision-making
- No built-in complexity assessment or task classification

Thanks for considering this — it would make Hermes significantly more practical for everyday use.

items.title: Bug: model picker ignores key_env on custom_providers list entries → '0 models listed for this provider'

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug

The model picker (`/model`, TUI **Set Main Model** dialog, Telegram/Discord inline picker) shows **"no models listed for this provider"** for `custom_providers:` list entries that authenticate via `key_env:` — even though the endpoint works correctly for chat completions.

Root cause: in `hermes_cli/model_switch.py`, the **Section 4** path that builds picker rows from `custom_providers:` list entries reads only the literal `api_key` field and never falls back to `os.environ[entry["key_env"]]`. The **Section 3** path (which serves `providers:` dict entries) does the fallback correctly. As a result, the picker calls `fetch_api_models(api_key=\"\", api_url=...)`, the endpoint returns 401, the exception is swallowed, and the row lands in the picker with `total_models = 0`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.14.0 (2026.5.16) — bug also present on `main` at the same line numbers as of this filing
- macOS 26.3 (Apple Silicon), Python 3.11.15
- Endpoint: a third-party OpenAI-compatible gateway (New API), `chat_completions` mode, requires bearer token

## Minimal repro

`~/.hermes/.env`:
```
NEW_API_KEY=sk-...
```

`~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
```yaml
model:
  default: deepseek-v4-flash
  provider: new-api

custom_providers:
  - name: new-api
    base_url: http://gateway.example/v1
    key_env: NEW_API_KEY
    api_mode: chat_completions
```

1. `hermes -z "hi"` → **works** (runtime path correctly resolves `key_env`)
2. Open TUI → **Set Main Model** dialog → row shows `new-api · custom:new-api · 0 models`, body says *"no models listed for this provider"*
3. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $NEW_API_KEY" http://gateway.example/v1/models` → returns full model catalog (so it's not an endpoint issue)

## Expected vs actual

| | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Picker call to `fetch_api_models` | `api_key` resolved from `os.environ[key_env]` | `api_key = ""` |
| `/v1/models` HTTP status | 200, list returned | 401, exception swallowed |
| Picker UI | full live model catalog | "0 models" / "no models listed for this provider" |

## Source location

`hermes_cli/model_switch.py`, Section 4 (handles `custom_providers:` **list**):

```python
# line 1591 (main + v0.14.0)
api_key = (entry.get("api_key") or "").strip()
```

compare with Section 3 (handles `providers:` **dict**) which does it correctly:

```python
# line 1522 (main + v0.14.0)
api_key = str(ep_cfg.get("api_key", "") or "").strip()
if not api_key:
    key_env = str(ep_cfg.get("key_env", "") or "").strip()
    api_key = os.environ.get(key_env, "").strip() if key_env else ""
```

The asymmetry means the same logical config (named OpenAI-compatible endpoint + `key_env`) works in one schema but silently fails in the other.

## Suggested fix

In `model_switch.py` around line 1591, port Section 3's fallback:

```python
api_key = (entry.get("api_key") or "").strip()
if not api_key:
    key_env = (entry.get("key_env") or "").strip()
    if key_env:
        api_key = os.environ.get(key_env, "").strip()
```

The downstream `should_probe` / `fetch_api_models` block (line ~1709) will then receive the real token and live discovery will succeed.

## Workarounds (for users hitting this today)

1. **Static models list** — populate `custom_providers[].models:` manually so the picker doesn't need live discovery:
   ```yaml
   custom_providers:
     - name: new-api
       base_url: http://gateway.example/v1
       key_env: NEW_API_KEY
       models:
         deepseek-v4-flash: {}
         gpt-5.4: {}
   ```
2. **Skip the picker** — set the model via CLI: `hermes config set model.default <name> && hermes gateway restart`

Neither workaround fixes the picker itself.

## Related

- #20582 — *"Model picker only shows one model for custom providers"*: same `custom_providers:` list path, related but distinct symptom (one-model vs zero-models). Reporter's endpoint was localhost without auth so they didn't trigger the `key_env` resolution gap. Likely both can be addressed in the same Section 4 cleanup.
- #8758 — *"named custom provider model discovery ignores models mapping and probe fallback"*: also touches Section 4 discovery logic.

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Environment
- **Hermes version**: v0.13.0 (a84cec61)
- **Provider**: Xiaomi MiMo
- **Model**: mimo-v2-omni
- **Endpoint**: https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1
- **OS**: macOS

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure Xiaomi MiMo as the main model:
   ```
   hermes model set mimo-v2-omni --provider xiaomi
   ```
2. Trigger a computer_use action, e.g.: "使用computer_use功能演示一下这个工具"
3. The model returns a tool call -> Hermes executes it and takes a screenshot
4. The tool result (containing image + text) is sent back to the API -> **400 error**

## Error
```
BadRequestError [HTTP 400]
Provider: xiaomi  Model: mimo-v2-omni
Endpoint: https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1
Error: HTTP 400: Param Incorrect
Details: {code: 400, message: Param Incorrect, param: `text` is not set, type: }
```

## Root cause analysis

### 1. Tool message format incompatible with Xiaomi API

When computer_use captures a screenshot, the tool result is an _multimodal dict that gets unwrapped at run_agent.py:10736-10740 into:

```json
{
  "role": "tool",
  "name": "computer_use",
  "content": [
    {"type": "text", "text": "capture mode=som ..."},
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}}
  ],
  "tool_call_id": "..."
}
```

Xiaomi API rejects this with `param: \`text\` is not set` --- it appears to require a top-level `text` field in the message, and does not accept `content` as an array for `tool`-role messages (even though it accepts image arrays for `user`-role messages).

### 2. Image rejection detection does not match Xiaomi error

run_agent.py:13096-13111 has a list of phrases to detect image rejection and auto-strip + retry:

```python
_IMAGE_REJECTION_PHRASES = (
    "only \"text\" content type is supported",
    "image_url is not supported",
    "multimodal is not supported",
    ...
)
```

Xiaomi error message `Param Incorrect: \`text\` is not set` does not match any of these phrases, so the automatic recovery path is never triggered.

### 3. Xiaomi provider has no custom transport adapter

plugins/model-providers/xiaomi/__init__.py only registers a basic ProviderProfile --- no custom message formatting or transport adapter to handle this API quirk.

## Note
- Normal vision analysis (user-role images) works perfectly with MiMo --- only tool-role messages with images fail
- MiMo mimo-v2-omni model advertises vision support, so the capability is there; the issue is purely on the message format compatibility

labels.name: P1

items.body:
## Description

When a board-specific `kanban.db` is corrupted (e.g., from a dispatcher crash mid-write) AND the top-level kanban DB (`~/.hermes/kanban/<board>.db`) is empty or missing, running any command that touches the board (e.g., `hermes kanban boards switch <board>`, `hermes kanban list`) silently recreates both databases from scratch — **with zero rows in all tables**. Full data loss.

## Timeline from a real incident (2026-05-22)

| Time (BRT) | Event |
|---|---|
| 14:07 | Dispatcher crashes with exception in `dispatch_once` (`kanban_db.py:4776`). DB write interrupted mid-operation |
| 15:43 | Gateway detects corrupted DB: "not a valid SQLite database; disabling dispatch" |
| 16:00 | Cron job runs `hermes kanban boards switch casalmaisfertil && hermes kanban list` |
| 16:02 | **New kanban.db created** (106KB, full schema, **0 rows in all tables**) |
| 16:03 | Gateway: "database changed; retrying dispatch" — resumes on empty board |

### Evidence

**15:43 — DB detected as invalid:**
```
ERROR gateway.run: kanban dispatcher: board casalmaisfertil database
/root/.hermes/kanban/boards/casalmaisfertil/kanban.db is not a valid SQLite database;
disabling dispatch for this board until the file changes or the gateway restarts.
```

**16:02 — New DB created without notify_subs table (race condition):**
```
WARNING gateway.run: kanban notifier tick failed: no such table: kanban_notify_subs
```

**16:03 — Dispatch resumes on empty board:**
```
INFO gateway.run: kanban dispatcher: board casalmaisfertil database changed; retrying dispatch
```

Aftermath: 7 tasks across 2 content waves, including dependencies, comments, run history — all lost. Reconstructed manually from memory and workspace artifacts.

## Root Cause

The top-level kanban DB was 0 bytes (never properly initialized or also corrupted). When commands encounter:
1. A top-level DB that is empty/invalid
2. A board DB that is corrupted/not valid SQLite

...the system **silently** initializes both from scratch, without:
- Attempting WAL/journal recovery
- Creating a backup of the corrupted file
- Emitting a warning
- Asking for confirmation

## Expected Behavior

1. **Never silently recreate a board DB.** Halt and require explicit `hermes kanban init`
2. **Attempt recovery first:** `PRAGMA integrity_check`, `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`
3. **Backup before wipe:** copy corrupted DB to `.bak` before recreating

## Related Issues

- #20055 — silently synthesizes boards from stale current-board pointer (same class of silent creation)
- #26479 — dispatcher handling of corrupted DBs (covers dispatcher, not silent recreation)
- #29507 — interrupted httpx thread corrupting kanban.db (similar corruption mechanism)

## Environment

- **Hermes:** v0.14.0 (2026.5.16), Python 3.11.15, Linux
- **Gateway embedded dispatcher:** `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway: true`
- **Board:** `casalmaisfertil` (non-default, ~7 tasks)

items.title: feat: channel-based model routing in gateway config
items.body:
## Problem Statement

Currently, Hermes uses a single model default per profile. When running a gateway instance connected to multiple Discord channels (or other platforms with multiple rooms/channels), there is no way to route different channels to different models without either:
- Running separate gateway instances per profile (high maintenance, config drift between profiles)
- Manually switching models per session via `/model` (not scalable, not automatic)

## Proposed Solution

Add a `routing` section to `config.yaml` that maps platform channel IDs to model overrides:

```yaml
routing:
  rules:
    - platform: discord
      channel_id: "1234567890"
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
      provider: anthropic

    - platform: discord
      channel_id: "9876543210"
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      provider: openrouter

  fallback:
    model: hermes-alt
    provider: custom
```

The gateway reads `source.channel_id` and `source.platform` on each incoming message, matches against rules top-down, and applies the matched model for that session. No profile switching, no separate gateway instances.

## Why This Matters

- Single gateway instance, multiple channels with different purposes (coding, casual, research) → different model strengths per use case
- No config drift — SOUL.md, skills, memory stay shared
- Consistent with how other routing systems work (nginx, 9router, etc.)

## Alternatives Considered

- **Profiles** — works but causes config drift; SOUL.md/skills must be manually synced or symlinked
- **Manual `/model` switching** — not automatic, not scalable
- **Patching `gateway/run.py`** — breaks on every `hermes update`

## Additional Context

- `source.channel_id` and `source.platform` are already available in the gateway message context, so the data needed for routing is already there
- Implementation could reuse the existing auxiliary model override pattern (`auxiliary.*.provider` + `auxiliary.*.model`) as a reference for how per-task model config works
